The November 2026 temperature anomaly off Southern California

The largest departure from normal in the CalCOFI record: what was measured, how it was checked and where it ranks

Author

CalCOFI

Published

2026-11-13

ImportantPreliminary data

The measurements from this cruise are preliminary: processed at sea, before final calibration (data_stage preliminary_with_bottle in release v2026.11.09). This analysis has not been peer reviewed. The checks under Is it real? are why the headline numbers are stated with confidence; their second decimal may change.

Summary

CalCOFI has measured the ocean off California at the same stations since 1949. Its fall 2026 cruise aboard R/V Sally Ride (31 October to 7 November 2026) found the largest departure from normal temperature in that record.

  • The measurement. On 31 October 2026, about 27 km off northern San Diego County (CalCOFI station 93.3 30.0), the water 40 to 50 m below the surface was 25.0 °C. The 1993–2013 November average at that station and depth is 12.2 °C.
  • The record. That departure, +12.8 °C, is the largest among the 581,071 station-and-depth values from 340 cruises (1950–2026) that have a baseline to compare with, which means the stations CalCOFI occupies today. The previous largest was +7.1 °C, on the same line in November 2015. The 1982–83 and 1997–98 El Niños peaked near +6 °C by the same measure. A cruder yardstick that reaches every station CalCOFI has ever occupied, the old lines off Baja California included, gives the same answer. The largest departure below the surface that a search of the literature found for the California Current, 8 to 8.7 °C off Baja California in October 1997 (Lynn et al. 1998; Durazo and Baumgartner 2002), is smaller too.
  • At the surface the departure is smaller. The sea surface was 5 to 8 °C warmer than normal at the 17 stations of the inner Southern California Bight and 1 to 4 °C warmer at the 18 stations seaward of them. The largest numbers are below the surface because the warm layer is unusually thick: water of 25 °C reached 55 m, where a normal November is already near 12 °C.
  • Averaged over the area sampled. Through the upper 50 m at the 32 stations sampled, the ocean was 5.1 °C warmer than normal. The previous high over those same stations was +3.4 °C (November 2015). At the peak of the 1997–98 El Niño it was +2.1 °C.
  • It is different water. The warm layer is also unusually salty (34.43–34.48, about 1.0 above normal): the mark of water from the subtropics, not of local water warmed in place. It is lighter than anything normally found at that station, and it has pressed the water beneath it about 100 m deeper than normal, which is what makes the departures at depth so large. Over the inner Bight the upper 50 m is 0.65 saltier than normal; the highest any earlier cruise found there is 0.38, at the peak of the 1997–98 El Niño, and the warm water of 2014–15 was not salty at all.
  • It has been checked. The instrument’s two temperature sensors agree within 0.01 °C through the warm layer, and its salinity matches water samples analysed on board. A buoy 2 km from one station read 25.1 °C when the instrument read 25.0 °C. The shore station on Scripps Pier recorded both the heat and the salt on its own instruments. Satellite analyses show the surface there about 5 °C above normal on the same day.
  • What it does not show. The cruise sampled 36 stations on CalCOFI’s three southern lines, off Southern California, and says nothing about waters farther north. The measurements show how warm the water is, not why: NOAA reports a strong El Niño in progress on top of a marine heatwave off California since 2025, and says the two cannot yet be separated.
TipDescribing it correctly
  • “12.8 °C warmer than normal” needs “at 40 to 50 m depth” beside it. At the sea surface the figure is 5 to 8 °C in the inner Southern California Bight.
  • For the region, the fair figure is the layer average: about 5 °C warmer than normal through the upper 50 m, against a previous record of 3.4 °C.
  • “Normal” is the 1993–2013 average for November at the same station and depth.
  • “The largest in CalCOFI’s record” means the largest departure from that normal at the stations CalCOFI occupies today, in a record that begins in 1949. It is a statement about these stations, not about the Pacific.
  • The data are preliminary.
code 
sf_use_s2(F)
land <- ne_countries(scale = 10, country = c("United States of America", "Mexico"), returnclass = "sf") |>
  st_crop(xmin = -127, xmax = -114, ymin = 28, ymax = 37)

pts <- d_sta |>
  filter(layer == "0-50 m", !is.na(anom)) |>
  transmute(site_key, line, station, lon, lat, z = anom)
stopifnot(min(pts$z) >= 0)   # the colour scale below starts at 0: nothing may hide under it

# the surface between the stations: the Explorer's own interpolator (ordinary kriging, calcofi4r::cc_interpolate()),
# drawn only inside the hull of the stations sampled (plus 15 km), never over land, and held inside the range of
# the measured values: the shading interpolates, it never extrapolates a gradient past the last station
srf  <- cc_interpolate(pts, method = "ok", cell_deg = 0.03, mask_km = 60, se = F)
hull <- st_as_sf(pts, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_union() |> st_convex_hull() |>
  st_transform(3310) |> st_buffer(15e3) |> st_transform(4326)
r    <- cc_interpolate_rast(srf)[["value"]] |>
  project("EPSG:4326") |>
  mask(vect(hull)) |>
  mask(vect(land), inverse = T)
d_r  <- as.data.frame(r, xy = T, na.rm = T) |>
  mutate(value = pmin(pmax(value, min(pts$z)), max(pts$z)))

# labels and palette ----

SITES    <- c("093.3 026.7", "093.3 028.0", "093.3 030.0", "093.3 035.0")
ZMAX     <- 160
lab_site <- function(x) glue("station {as.numeric(sub('.* ', '', x))}")

d_2026 <- q("
  SELECT site_key, depth_m, avg(value) AS temp FROM cast_1m
  WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND direction = 'd' AND measurement_qual IS NULL
    AND site_key IN ({SITES*}) AND depth_m <= {ZMAX}
  GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY site_key, depth_m")
d_norm <- q("
  SELECT site_key, depth_bin + 5 AS depth_m, clim_mean AS temp, clim_sd AS sd, n_cruises FROM climatology
  WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND month = 11 AND clim_mean IS NOT NULL
    AND depth_bin IS NOT NULL AND site_key IN ({SITES*}) AND depth_bin + 5 <= {ZMAX}
  ORDER BY site_key, depth_bin")
d_prev <- q("
  SELECT site_key, cruise_key, cruise_year AS yr, depth_bin + 5 AS depth_m, v AS temp FROM cell
  WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND cruise_month = 11 AND cruise_key <> {CRUISE}
    AND site_key IN ({SITES*}) AND depth_bin + 5 <= {ZMAX}
  ORDER BY site_key, cruise_key, depth_bin")
d_peak <- d_cell26 |>
  filter(site_key %in% SITES) |>
  group_by(site_key) |> slice_max(anom, n = 1) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(depth_m = depth_bin + 5)
d_lab <- tibble(
  site_key = SITES[1], temp = 15.2, depth_m = c(96, 108, 120, 138),
  label    = c("31 Oct – 1 Nov 2026", "November 2015", "November normal\n1993–2013, ± 1 sd", "every other November"),
  col      = c(COL_2026, COL_2015, COL_NORM, STONE),
  lw       = c(1.1, 0.8, 0.9, 0.35))

ggplot(mapping = aes(temp, depth_m)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = d_norm, aes(xmin = temp - sd, xmax = temp + sd), fill = COL_NORM, alpha = 0.15, orientation = "y") +
  geom_path(data = filter(d_prev, yr != 2015), aes(group = cruise_key), colour = STONE, linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_path(data = filter(d_prev, yr == 2015), aes(group = cruise_key), colour = COL_2015, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_path(data = d_norm, colour = COL_NORM, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_path(data = d_2026, colour = COL_2026, linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_segment(
    data = d_peak, aes(x = clim_mean, xend = v, yend = depth_m), colour = INK, linewidth = 0.4,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(4, "pt"), ends = "both")) +
  geom_text(data = d_peak, aes(x = (clim_mean + v) / 2, y = depth_m - 5, label = paste(fs(anom), "°C")), colour = INK, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(data = d_lab, aes(label = label), colour = INK, size = 3.1, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.8, lineheight = 0.9) +
  geom_segment(data = d_lab, aes(x = temp - 3.4, xend = temp - 0.6, yend = depth_m), colour = d_lab$col, linewidth = d_lab$lw) +
  facet_wrap(~ site_key, nrow = 1, labeller = as_labeller(lab_site)) +
  scale_y_reverse(limits = c(ZMAX, 0), expand = c(0, 0), breaks = seq(0, ZMAX, 20)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(9, 27.5), breaks = seq(10, 26, 4), position = "top") +
  labs(
    title    = "Line 93.3 off San Diego County: a 25 °C layer reaches 55 m, where the water is normally 12 °C",
    subtitle = glue("Temperature (°C) against depth (m), {trimws(format(min(sfc$t0[sfc$site_key %in% SITES]), '%e %B'))} – {trimws(format(max(sfc$t0[sfc$site_key %in% SITES]), '%e %B %Y'))}, beside the November normal and every other November cruise ({min(d_prev$yr)}–{max(d_prev$yr)})"),
    x = NULL, y = "Depth (m)",
    caption  = glue(
      "Normal: the 1993–2013 mean per 10 m depth bin for cruises whose month is November ({min(d_norm$n_cruises)}–{max(d_norm$n_cruises)} cruises at these stations). The arrow is each station's largest measured departure.\n",
      "CalCOFI CTD, R/V Sally Ride; CalCOFI Integrated Database release {VER} (doi:{CAT$doi}). Preliminary data.  calcofi.io")) +
  theme_story() +
  theme(panel.spacing = unit(14, "pt"))

In thirty seconds

The same data as an animation, without sound: the nine November cruises behind the normal, the normal itself, each November since 2014 as its difference from that normal on one fixed colour scale, and the section of line 93.3 under the sea surface. It is also on YouTube, and the file can be downloaded (5.7 MB, 1920 × 1080), as can its last frame. How it is made is under Code.

1 What CalCOFI measures, and what “normal” means here

The California Cooperative Oceanic Fisheries Investigations (CalCOFI) has occupied a fixed grid of stations off California since 1949, four times a year in recent decades (Bograd et al. 2003; McClatchie 2014). At each station a CTD (an instrument that records conductivity, temperature and depth) is lowered to about 500 m, and water is collected in bottles at about 20 depths. The stations sit on numbered lines that run offshore from the coast: line 93.3 leaves the coast north of San Diego, line 90.0 at Dana Point and line 86.7 near Santa Monica Bay.

This page uses the CalCOFI Integrated Database, release v2026.11.09 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24083894), in which two temperature series reach back through the record:

  • the CTD series (temperature_ave, the average of the instrument’s two sensors), 1993–2026, with a value every 10 m;
  • the bottle series (temperature), 1949–2021, at the bottle depths.

Normal is the release’s own climatology table: for each station, each 10 m depth bin and each calendar month, the mean of everything measured there on cruises of that month during 1993–2013, kept only where at least five cruises contribute. A departure (an anomaly) is a measurement minus the normal of its own station, depth and month. It is the same baseline the Explorer and the CTD transects subtract. Where no normal exists a departure is left blank; it is never treated as zero.

The fall cruise does not sail in the same month every year, and that matters for what follows. “November” on this page means the cruises whose median cast date falls in November.

2 The measurement

2.1 Line 93.3, bin by bin

The section plot that first showed the anomaly draws contours, which are interpolated between stations. The table below is what was measured: each 10 m depth bin at the four inshore stations of line 93.3, beside the normal for that bin and the number of 1993–2013 November cruises the normal averages.

code 
d_bins <- d_cell26 |>
  filter(line == 93.3, station <= 35, depth_bin <= 100) |>
  arrange(station, depth_bin) |>
  transmute(
    station = site_key, `depth (m)` = glue("{depth_bin}–{depth_bin + 10}"),
    `observed (°C)` = round(v, 2), `normal (°C)` = round(clim_mean, 2), `normal sd` = round(clim_sd, 2),
    `baseline cruises` = n_cruises, `departure (°C)` = round(anom, 2),
    `departure from the Sep–Nov normal (°C)` = round(anom_season, 2))
dt_(d_bins, caption = "Measured 10 m bins on line 93.3, stations 26.7 to 35, fall 2026.")
  • The largest measured departure is +12.81 °C (station 30, 40–50 m: 25.00 °C against 12.19 °C). The next station inshore reaches +12.51 °C at 50–60 m and +12.39 °C at 40–50 m. The “12” on the contour plot is measured; it is not made by interpolation.
  • The normal behind each bin is 6 to 8 November cruises.
  • Against the seasonal normal (September to November, 19 cruises) the largest departure is still +11.86 °C.
code 
d_sec <- q("
  SELECT site_key, station, depth_bin, v AS observed, clim_mean AS normal, anom AS difference FROM cell
  WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND line = 93.3 AND depth_bin < 200
  ORDER BY station, depth_bin") |>
  mutate(km = (station - 26.4) * KM_PER_STATION, depth_m = depth_bin + 5)
d_stn  <- distinct(d_sec, station, km)
grid_x <- seq(min(d_sec$km), max(d_sec$km), by = 1)
# along the line, at each depth bin: linear between the stations that have a value there, never beyond them
along <- function(col) d_sec |>
  filter(!is.na(.data[[col]])) |>
  group_by(depth_m) |> filter(n() >= 2) |>
  reframe(value = approx(km, .data[[col]], xout = grid_x, rule = 1)$y, km = grid_x) |>
  filter(!is.na(value))

sec_panel <- function(col, title, pal, lim, brk, legend, top = NULL, bottom = NULL) {
  d <- along(col)
  ggplot(d, aes(km, depth_m)) +
    geom_raster(aes(fill = value), interpolate = T) +
    geom_contour(aes(z = value), breaks = seq(-20, 40, 2), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_point(data = d_stn, aes(km, 0), shape = 25, size = 2, fill = INK, colour = INK, inherit.aes = F) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colours = pal, limits = lim, breaks = brk, oob = scales::squish, name = legend,
      guide = guide_colourbar(barheight = unit(95, "pt"), barwidth = unit(8, "pt"), frame.colour = STONE, ticks.colour = "white")) +
    scale_x_reverse(
      expand = c(0, 0), name = bottom,
      sec.axis = dup_axis(breaks = d_stn$km, labels = d_stn$station, name = top)) +
    scale_y_reverse(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(200, -6), breaks = seq(0, 200, 50)) +
    labs(subtitle = title, y = "Depth (m)") +
    theme_story() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9), legend.text = element_text(size = 8.5, colour = MUTED),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = INK, face = "bold", size = rel(0.95), margin = margin(b = 2)),
      axis.title.x.top = element_text(size = 9, colour = MUTED, hjust = 0), axis.title.x.bottom = element_text(size = 10.5),
      panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#eef0f2", colour = NA))}

pal_temp <- cmocean("thermal")(256)
p_norm <- sec_panel("normal",     "The November normal, 1993–2013",             pal_temp, c(8, 26), seq(8, 26, 6), "°C", top = "station")
p_obs  <- sec_panel("observed",   "Measured, 31 October – 1 November 2026",      pal_temp, c(8, 26), seq(8, 26, 6), "°C")
p_diff <- sec_panel("difference", "The difference: how much warmer than normal", pal_warm, c(0, ANOM_MAX), seq(0, 12, 3), "°C above\nnormal",
                    bottom = "Distance offshore along the line (km)")
stopifnot(min(d_sec$difference, na.rm = T) > -0.5)   # the warm-only scale hides nothing below zero

times <- c("twice", "three times", "four times", "five times")[floor(mean(d_mld$mld) / mean(d_mld$clim)) - 1]
p_norm / p_obs / p_diff +
  plot_annotation(
    title   = glue("Line 93.3: the warm surface layer is more than {times} its normal thickness"),
    caption = glue("CalCOFI CTD, 10 m depth bins; CalCOFI Integrated Database release {VER} (doi:{CAT$doi}). Preliminary data.  calcofi.io"),
    theme   = theme_story())

2.2 What kind of anomaly this is

Read the profiles before the numbers. At stations 26.7, 28 and 30 the cruise found a mixed layer of about 25 °C reaching 55–57 m (by a density criterion of 0.125 kg m⁻³, one of the standard thresholds (Levitus 1982; Boyer Montégut et al. 2004); the November normal there is 15–17 m). Below it the temperature falls steeply. The departure peaks at 40–60 m because that is where a normal November has already dropped into the cold water of the thermocline. The sea surface was about 7 °C above normal; the thickness of the layer adds the rest.

The water is also a different water mass. Salinity in the layer is 34.43–34.48 at stations 28 and 30, 0.94 to 1.16 above the November normal, where the normal’s own standard deviation is about 0.11. Warming the local surface layer does not change its salt. The water mass takes this up below.

2.3 One spot, 76 years

code 
d_hist <- q("
  SELECT cruise_key, dataset_key, cruise_year, cruise_month, datetime, v, anom, clim_mean FROM cell
  WHERE site_key = {k$top_site} AND depth_bin = {k$top_bin}") |>
  mutate(
    date   = as.Date(datetime),
    series = if_else(dataset_key == "calcofi_bottle", "bottle", "CTD"),
    nov    = cruise_month == 11)
h_prev <- d_hist |> filter(cruise_key != CRUISE) |> slice_max(v, n = 1, with_ties = F)
h_lab  <- bind_rows(
  d_hist |> filter(cruise_key == CRUISE) |> mutate(label = glue("{format(date, '%e %b %Y') |> trimws()}: {f1(v)} °C")),
  h_prev |> mutate(label = glue("{format(date, '%e %b %Y') |> trimws()}: {f1(v)} °C")))

ggplot(d_hist, aes(date, v)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = k$top_clim, colour = COL_NORM, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, !nov), colour = STONE, size = 1.1, alpha = 0.7) +
  annotate("label", x = as.Date("1968-06-01"), y = k$top_clim, label = glue("November normal {f1(k$top_clim)} °C"), colour = INK, fill = "white", size = 3.2, linewidth = 0, border.colour = NA) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, nov), aes(shape = series), colour = COL_NORM, size = 2.2, stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, cruise_key == CRUISE), colour = COL_2026, size = 3.4) +
  geom_text(data = h_lab, aes(label = label), colour = INK, size = 3.4, hjust = 1, nudge_x = -500, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(bottle = 1, CTD = 16)) +
  scale_x_date(breaks = as.Date(paste0(seq(1950, 2020, 10), "-01-01")), date_labels = "%Y", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.03))) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(10, 26, 4)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Station 93.3 30.0, 40–50 m depth: nothing like it in any month since 1950",
    subtitle = glue("Temperature (°C) on {n_distinct(d_hist$cruise_key)} cruises. Colour: November cruises (open: bottle, filled: CTD). Grey: every other month."),
    x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_story()

Across all months, 265 cruises since 1950 have sampled this depth at this station. The warmest before this cruise was 18.11 °C (29 October 2015, on the November 2015 cruise).

3 Is it real?

A 12.8 °C departure is the first thing an oceanographer will challenge. These are the checks, from the instrument outward.

3.1 The data’s stage and its quality flags

code 
d_stage <- q("
  SELECT data_stage, count(*) AS casts FROM sample
  WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND sample_type = 'cast' GROUP BY ALL")
d_flag <- q("
  SELECT f.measurement_type, f.measurement_qual AS flag, count(*) AS values, count(DISTINCT f.sample_key) AS casts,
         min(f.depth_min_m) AS depth_min_m, max(f.depth_min_m) AS depth_max_m,
         string_agg(DISTINCT s.site_key, ', ' ORDER BY s.site_key) AS stations
  FROM obs_ctd_full f JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
  WHERE f.measurement_qual IS NOT NULL AND f.measurement_type LIKE 'temperature%'
  GROUP BY ALL")
n_prelim <- q("SELECT count(*) AS n, min(cruise_key) AS first FROM cruise_ref WHERE ctd_stage LIKE 'preliminary%'")
kable(d_flag, caption = "Every flagged temperature value on the cruise (CTD codes: 8 questionable, 9 bad or missing).")

All 72 casts of the cruise (36 stations, down and up) carry data_stage preliminary_with_bottle: one-metre averages processed at sea, before final calibration. So does every CTD cruise since 2021-07-33P4 in this release (22 cruises). The only flagged temperatures are on one up cast, on the primary sensor, and the sensor-pair average the analysis uses already leaves them out. Nothing on line 93.3 is flagged.

3.2 Two sensors, two passes

code 
d_pair <- q("
  SELECT a.site_key, a.direction, a.depth_m, a.value AS t1, b.value AS t2
  FROM cast_1m a JOIN cast_1m b USING (sample_key, depth_m)
  WHERE a.measurement_type = 'temperature_1' AND b.measurement_type = 'temperature_2'
    AND a.measurement_qual IS NULL AND b.measurement_qual IS NULL")
d_du <- q("
  SELECT site_key, depth_m, max(value) FILTER (WHERE direction = 'd') AS down, max(value) FILTER (WHERE direction = 'u') AS up
  FROM cast_1m WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND measurement_qual IS NULL GROUP BY ALL") |>
  filter(!is.na(down), !is.na(up))
d_gap <- q("
  SELECT site_key, date_diff('minute', min(datetime) FILTER (WHERE direction = 'd'), max(datetime) FILTER (WHERE direction = 'u')) AS minutes
  FROM cast_1m WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND depth_m <= 40 AND site_key IN ({core*}) GROUP BY site_key")
chk <- list(
  pair_all  = d_pair |> filter(depth_m <= 100) |> summarize(n = n(), mean = mean(t1 - t2), p99 = quantile(abs(t1 - t2), 0.99)),
  pair_core = d_pair |> filter(site_key %in% core, depth_m <= 50) |> summarize(n = n(), max = max(abs(t1 - t2)), median = median(abs(t1 - t2))),
  du_core   = d_du   |> filter(site_key %in% core, depth_m <= 40) |> summarize(n = n(), mean = mean(abs(down - up)), max = max(abs(down - up))),
  du_base   = d_du   |> filter(site_key %in% core, between(depth_m, 50, 65)) |> summarize(max = max(abs(down - up))),
  gap       = range(d_gap$minutes))

The CTD carries two independent temperature sensors. Through the warm layer at stations 28 and 30 (the top 50 m, 200 one-metre values) they never differ by more than 0.006 °C; half of the values differ by 0.4 thousandths of a degree or less. Over every cast of the cruise, in the top 100 m, their mean difference is 0.0025 °C.

Each station is also measured twice, on the way down and on the way up. At those two stations the two passes through the top 40 m are 46 to 48 minutes apart and differ by 0.05 °C on average. At the base of the layer (50–65 m) they differ by up to 1.4 °C: internal waves lift and drop that boundary by a few metres within the hour. That moves the 50–60 m bin. It does not move the 40–50 m bin, which lies inside the layer on both passes.

3.3 Bottles: salinity and oxygen

code 
d_btl <- q("
  SELECT site_key, depth_m,
         max(value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave')   AS t,
         max(value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'salinity_1')        AS s_ctd,
         max(value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'salinity_btl')      AS s_btl,
         max(value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'sigma_theta_1')     AS sigma,
         max(value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'oxygen_btl_ml_l')   AS o2_btl
  FROM cast_1m WHERE direction = 'u' AND site_key IN ({core*}) AND depth_m <= 60
  GROUP BY ALL HAVING s_btl IS NOT NULL OR o2_btl IS NOT NULL ORDER BY site_key, depth_m") |>
  left_join(
    d_cell26 |> transmute(site_key, depth_bin, t_normal = clim_mean),
    by = join_by(site_key, closest(depth_m >= depth_bin))) |>
  mutate(
    # oxygen solubility (Garcia & Gordon 1992, via gsw), umol/kg -> mL/L
    o2_sat        = gsw_O2sol_SP_pt(s_ctd, t)        * (1000 + sigma) / 1000 / 44.66,
    o2_sat_normal = gsw_O2sol_SP_pt(s_ctd, t_normal) * (1000 + sigma) / 1000 / 44.66)
d_btl |>
  transmute(
    station = site_key, `depth (m)` = depth_m, `CTD temperature (°C)` = round(t, 2),
    `CTD salinity` = round(s_ctd, 3), `bottle salinity` = round(s_btl, 3), difference = round(s_btl - s_ctd, 3),
    `bottle oxygen (mL/L)` = round(o2_btl, 2), `saturation at the measured temperature` = round(o2_sat, 2),
    `saturation at the normal temperature` = round(o2_sat_normal, 2)) |>
  kable(caption = "Water samples from the warm layer at stations 28 and 30, beside the CTD on the up cast.")

Salinity is measured twice by unrelated methods: the CTD computes it from conductivity and temperature, and a salinometer measures it on the bottled water samples in the ship’s laboratory. In the warm layer the two agree to within 0.002. A temperature error of only 0.1 °C would shift the CTD’s salinity by 0.08 and break that agreement; an error of several degrees is out of the question.

The oxygen titrated from the same bottles (4.79–4.89 mL/L down to 50 m) is what a mixed layer in contact with the air holds at 25 °C (saturation 4.75 mL/L). Water at the normal temperature of those depths would hold about 5.7 mL/L.

3.4 The baseline: is the normal the right normal?

code 
# the record cell against every reasonable definition of its normal
b_cells <- q("
  SELECT cruise_key, cruise_year, v, n_obs FROM cell
  WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND site_key = {k$top_site} AND depth_bin = {k$top_bin} AND cruise_month = 11 AND cruise_key <> {CRUISE}")
b_in  <- b_cells |> filter(between(cruise_year, 1993, 2013))
b_loo <- map_dbl(seq_len(nrow(b_in)), \(i) with(b_in[-i, ], sum(v * n_obs) / sum(n_obs)))
b_btl <- q("
  SELECT clim_mean, n_cruises FROM climatology
  WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature' AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle' AND site_key = {k$top_site} AND depth_bin = {k$top_bin} AND month = 11")
# the same baseline cruises from their FULL one-metre casts (obs_ctd_full), not the thinned series the normal is built from
release_view("obs_ctd_full", parts = b_in$cruise_key, name = "obs_ctd_full_base")
b_full <- q("
  SELECT f.cruise_key, avg(f.measurement_value) AS v, count(*) AS n
  FROM obs_ctd_full_base f JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
  WHERE f.measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND f.measurement_qual IS NULL AND s.site_key = {k$top_site}
    AND f.depth_min_m >= {k$top_bin} AND f.depth_min_m < {k$top_bin + 10}
  GROUP BY f.cruise_key")
stopifnot(nrow(b_full) == nrow(b_in))
# fall 2026 from its own one-metre casts, for the row that uses one-metre normals (like with like)
v26_full <- q("
  SELECT avg(value) AS v FROM cast_1m
  WHERE site_key = {k$top_site} AND measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND measurement_qual IS NULL
    AND depth_m >= {k$top_bin} AND depth_m < {k$top_bin + 10}")$v
d_base <- tribble(
  ~`definition of normal`,                                                             ~cruises,                ~normal,          ~value,
  "the release's climatology: every 1993–2013 November value in the bin (used on this page)", top$n_cruises,     top$clim_mean,    top$v,
  "the same cruises, one value per cruise",                                            nrow(b_in),               mean(b_in$v),     top$v,
  "the same cruises and fall 2026 from their full one-metre casts, not the thinned series", nrow(b_full),        mean(b_full$v),   v26_full,
  "leaving out each baseline cruise in turn: the lowest normal",                       nrow(b_in) - 1L,          min(b_loo),       top$v,
  "leaving out each baseline cruise in turn: the highest normal",                      nrow(b_in) - 1L,          max(b_loo),       top$v,
  "every earlier November cruise with a CTD cast, to 2025, one value per cruise",      nrow(b_cells),            mean(b_cells$v),  top$v,
  "the bottle series' own climatology for the cell",                                   b_btl$n_cruises,          b_btl$clim_mean,  top$v,
  "the release's seasonal normal (September to November)",                             top$season_n_cruises,     top$season_mean,  top$v) |>
  mutate(`normal (°C)` = round(normal, 2), `fall 2026 (°C)` = round(value, 2), `departure (°C)` = round(value - normal, 2)) |>
  select(-normal, -value)
kable(d_base, caption = glue("The departure at the record cell (station 93.3 30.0, 40–50 m) under {nrow(d_base)} definitions of normal."))

The normal is thin, 6 cruises at this cell, so the table asks how much the answer depends on it. Under every definition the departure is between 11.4 and 13.0 °C.

Timing within the season is the other way a baseline can mislead. The cruise worked the inshore end of line 93.3 on 31 October and 1 November. The 8 cruises behind the November normal there were on station between 25 October and 11 November (median 4 November), so the cruise sits inside their range, about 4 days ahead of its middle. The surface normal falls by about 2 °C from October to November, so the calendar can account for a few tenths of a degree at the surface, not more. The seasonal normal in the last row is the conservative bound.

3.5 The thinned series against the full profile

The release’s main table keeps a thinned CTD series (a value every 10 m plus the points where the profile bends), and the normal was built from the same series. The check is whether a 10 m bin mean of the thinned series stands for the full one-metre profile.

code 
d_thin <- q("
  WITH f AS (
    SELECT site_key, CAST(floor(depth_m / 10) * 10 AS INTEGER) AS depth_bin, avg(value) AS v_full
    FROM cast_1m WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND measurement_qual IS NULL AND direction = 'd' GROUP BY ALL)
  SELECT c.site_key, c.depth_bin, c.v, f.v_full, c.v - f.v_full AS diff
  FROM cell c JOIN f USING (site_key, depth_bin) WHERE c.cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND c.depth_bin < 200")
thin <- d_thin |> summarize(n = n(), mean = mean(diff), p95 = quantile(abs(diff), 0.95), max = max(abs(diff)))
thin_top <- d_thin |> filter(site_key == k$top_site, depth_bin == k$top_bin)

Over the 588 bins of the cruise above 200 m, the thinned bin mean differs from the full down-cast mean by +0.08 °C on average, and by less than 0.29 °C in 95 % of bins (the largest differences are in the thermocline, where a few points stand for a steep gradient). At the record cell the two are 25.00 and 24.97 °C.

code 
# the same comparison on the six baseline cruises read at one metre, at the cruise's stations, bins 10 to 40 m
d_thinb <- q("
  WITH f AS (
    SELECT o.cruise_key, s.site_key, CAST(floor(o.depth_min_m / 10) * 10 AS INTEGER) AS depth_bin, avg(o.measurement_value) AS v_full
    FROM obs_ctd_full_base o JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
    WHERE o.measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND o.measurement_qual IS NULL AND o.depth_min_m < 50 GROUP BY ALL)
  SELECT c.depth_bin, count(*) AS cells, avg(c.v - f.v_full) AS thinned_minus_1m, avg(c.depth_m - c.depth_bin) AS m_below_bin_top
  FROM cell c JOIN f USING (cruise_key, site_key, depth_bin)
  WHERE c.dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND c.depth_bin BETWEEN 10 AND 40 AND c.site_key IN ({unique(d_sta$site_key)*})
  GROUP BY c.depth_bin ORDER BY c.depth_bin")

In stratified water the thinned bin mean runs a little warm. In the six baseline cruises read at one metre, at these stations, it is 0.09 to 0.22 °C warmer than the one-metre bin mean in the bins between 10 and 50 m, because its points sit 2.6 m below the top of the bin on average where a one-metre series sits 4.5 m. The normal is built from that same thinned series, so a departure on this page compares like with like. A departure computed from one-metre values against this normal reads low by that amount in ordinary, stratified years; in fall 2026, when the upper 50 m was mixed, the two agree.

3.6 Are the stations where they should be?

code 
d_pos <- q("
  WITH h AS (
    SELECT site_key, median(latitude) AS lat0, median(longitude) AS lon0, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS n_cruises
    FROM cell WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE} AND depth_bin = 0 GROUP BY site_key)
  SELECT c.site_key, c.latitude, c.longitude, h.lat0, h.lon0, h.n_cruises
  FROM cell c JOIN h USING (site_key) WHERE c.cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND c.depth_bin = 0") |>
  mutate(km = as.numeric(st_distance(
    st_as_sf(pick(longitude, latitude), coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326),
    st_as_sf(pick(lon0, lat0), coords = c("lon0", "lat0"), crs = 4326), by_element = T)) / 1000)

A cast filed under the wrong station would be compared with the wrong normal. Each of the cruise’s 36 stations with a history lies within 3.2 km of the median position of every earlier occupation of that station (median 0.09 km).

3.7 Buoys

code 
# the cast list the outside-sources script reads: one row per station, from the release
d_casts <- q("
  WITH c AS (
    SELECT sample_key, site_key, min(datetime) AS t0, avg(latitude) AS lat, avg(longitude) AS lon,
           avg(value) FILTER (WHERE depth_m <= 3) AS t_top3m, avg(value) FILTER (WHERE depth_m < 10) AS t_0_10m, max(depth_m) AS zmax
    FROM cast_1m WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND measurement_qual IS NULL AND direction = 'd' GROUP BY ALL)
  SELECT site_key, replace(sample_key, 'calcofi_ctd-cast:cast:', '') AS cast_id, strftime(t0, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ') AS time_utc,
         round(lat, 4) AS lat, round(lon, 4) AS lon, round(t_top3m, 3) AS ctd_t_top3m, round(t_0_10m, 3) AS ctd_t_0_10m, zmax
  FROM c ORDER BY t0")
write_csv(d_casts, file.path(DIR_DATA, "casts.csv"), na = "")

# the outside sources are fetched once by scripts/temperature_anomaly_outside_sources.py (NDBC keeps 45 days only)
# and kept in the repo; a missing file means that script has not been run
f_out <- file.path(DIR_DATA, c("buoy_stations.csv", "buoys_at_casts.csv", "buoy_series.csv", "satellite_at_casts.csv", "argo_profiles.csv", "sources.csv", "pier_daily.csv", "glider_index.csv"))
stopifnot("run scripts/temperature_anomaly_outside_sources.py first" = all(file.exists(f_out)))
buoy_name <- function(x) str_remove(x, ",? CA\\b.*$") |> str_to_title()   # "Torrey Pines Outer, CA (100)" -> "Torrey Pines Outer"
d_bstn  <- read_csv(f_out[1]) |> mutate(name = buoy_name(name))
d_bpair <- read_csv(f_out[2]) |> mutate(buoy_name = buoy_name(buoy_name))
d_bser  <- read_csv(f_out[3]) |> mutate(time = as.POSIXct(hour_utc, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ", tz = "UTC"))
d_sat   <- read_csv(f_out[4])
d_argo  <- read_csv(f_out[5])
d_osrc  <- read_csv(f_out[6])
d_pier  <- read_csv(f_out[7]) |> mutate(yr = as.integer(format(date, "%Y")), md = format(date, "%m-%d"))
d_gl    <- read_csv(f_out[8], col_types = "cd") |> mutate(date = as.Date(paste0(month, "-15")))

Moored buoys report water temperature near the surface every half hour, through the National Data Buoy Center. They are operated by other programs (most of these by the Coastal Data Information Program at Scripps (Coastal Data Information Program 1975)) and share nothing with the ship’s instruments. The table pairs each cast with every buoy within 15 km, at the buoy report nearest in time.

code 
d_bpair |>
  transmute(
    station = site_key, `cast (UTC)` = sub("T", " ", sub(":\\d\\dZ$", "", cast_time_utc)),
    `CTD, top 3 m (°C)` = round(ctd_t_top3m, 2), buoy = glue("{buoy_name} ({buoy})"), `km apart` = km_apart,
    `buoy (°C)` = buoy_wtmp, `buoy − CTD (°C)` = buoy_minus_ctd,
    `buoy range, ±12 h (°C)` = glue("{buoy_24h_min}–{buoy_24h_max}")) |>
  kable(caption = "Buoy water temperature beside the CTD (buoys report to 0.1 °C).")

The closest pair is 2.3 km and a few minutes apart: the Torrey Pines Outer buoy read 25.1 °C when the CTD read 25.00 °C at station 093.3 028.0. The buoy nearest each of 7 casts (2–13 km away) reads within 0.6 °C of the CTD, including the cool side of the front (19.1 °C at San Nicolas Island against the CTD’s 19.07 °C). Pairs farther apart differ by up to 1.2 °C, which is the front itself.

code 
SHOW <- c("46225", "46254", "46219", "46047")
d_b  <- d_bser |> filter(buoy %in% SHOW) |>
  left_join(select(d_bstn, buoy, name), by = "buoy") |>
  mutate(buoy = factor(buoy, SHOW))
col_b  <- setNames(c("#b3261e", "#c69214", "#00629b", "#457a1c"), SHOW)
d_end  <- d_b |> group_by(buoy, name) |> slice_max(time, n = 1) |> ungroup()
d_ctd  <- d_bpair |> filter(buoy %in% SHOW) |> group_by(buoy) |> slice_min(km_apart, n = 1) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(time = as.POSIXct(cast_time_utc, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC"), buoy = factor(buoy, SHOW))

ggplot(d_b, aes(time, wtmp, colour = buoy)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = as.POSIXct(cr$date_min, tz = "UTC"), xmax = as.POSIXct(cr$date_max + 1, tz = "UTC"), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = SAND) +
  annotate("text", x = as.POSIXct(cr$date_min, tz = "UTC") + 3.5 * 86400, y = 26.2, label = "the cruise", colour = MUTED, size = 3.1) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = d_ctd, aes(y = ctd_t_top3m), shape = 21, fill = "white", colour = INK, size = 2.6, stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = d_end, aes(label = name), colour = INK, hjust = 0, direction = "y", nudge_x = 1.2 * 86400, size = 3.2,
    segment.colour = MUTED, segment.size = 0.2, min.segment.length = 0, seed = 1, xlim = c(max(d_b$time) + 86400, NA)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = col_b) +
  scale_x_datetime(date_breaks = "1 week", date_labels = "%e %b", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.22))) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(18, 26, 2)) +
  labs(
    title    = "The warm water was there for weeks, and the cool water offshore stayed cool",
    subtitle = "Water temperature (°C), hourly means. White dots: the CTD's top 3 m at the nearest cast.",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption  = "Buoy data from CDIP, Scripps Institution of Oceanography (cdip.ucsd.edu), and NOAA National Data Buoy Center, through NDBC realtime files, read 13 November 2026.") +
  theme_story()

3.8 Scripps Pier

The shore station on Scripps Pier in La Jolla has its own instruments in the water at the coast and reports temperature and salinity every few minutes (the SCCOOS automated shore station, running since 2013). These are its daily means, of the values that pass the station’s own quality tests. The pier’s much longer manual record, kept daily since 1916 (Carter et al. 2022; Rasmussen et al. 2020), is taken up under context.

code 
WIN <- c("08-01", "11-12")
p_long <- d_pier |>
  filter(md >= WIN[1], md <= WIN[2], md != "02-29") |>
  pivot_longer(c(temp, sal), names_to = "var", values_to = "value") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(day = as.Date(paste0("2026-", md)), var = factor(var, c("temp", "sal"), c("Temperature (°C)", "Salinity")))
p_rng <- p_long |> filter(yr < 2026) |> group_by(var, day) |>
  summarize(lo = min(value), hi = max(value), mid = median(value), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |> filter(n >= 8)
p_26  <- p_long |> filter(yr == 2026)

pier_panel <- function(v, ylim, breaks) {
  ggplot(filter(p_26, var == v), aes(day)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = cr$date_min, xmax = cr$date_max + 1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = SAND) +
    geom_ribbon(data = filter(p_rng, var == v), aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = STONE, alpha = 0.45) +
    geom_line(data = filter(p_rng, var == v), aes(y = mid), colour = MUTED, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_line(aes(y = value), colour = COL_2026, linewidth = 0.9) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 weeks", date_labels = "%e %b", expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = breaks) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = ylim) +          # the band may leave the axis: a few earlier days dip far below it
    labs(subtitle = v, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_story() +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = INK, face = "bold", size = rel(0.95), margin = margin(b = 2)))}
s_low    <- p_rng |> filter(var == "Salinity") |> pull(lo) |> min()
s_low_26 <- p_26  |> filter(var == "Salinity") |> slice_min(value, n = 1, with_ties = F)

(pier_panel("Temperature (°C)", c(14, 26), seq(14, 26, 4)) + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())) /
  pier_panel("Salinity", c(32.8, 34.4), seq(33, 34.4, 0.4)) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "At Scripps Pier, on other instruments: the same heat and the same salt",
    subtitle = glue("Daily means. Red: 2026. Grey: the range and median of the same calendar day, {min(d_pier$yr)}–2025."),
    caption  = glue(
      "The salinity axis is cut at 32.8: the earlier range dips below it on some days (to {f1(s_low)}), and so does 2026 in late August (to {f1(s_low_26$value)} on {trimws(format(s_low_26$day, '%e %B'))}).\n",
      "SCCOOS automated shore station, Scripps Pier (Scripps Institution of Oceanography), through the IOOS sensors ERDDAP, read 13 November 2026."),
    theme    = theme_story())

On 5 November the pier’s daily mean was 24.14 °C. The highest for that calendar day in the 13 earlier years of the record was 19.85 °C (2014). The pier’s warmest day on record, 25.62 °C, came in August 2018, in high summer.

Salinity is the sharper signal. Before June 2026 the pier’s daily salinity had a median of 33.43 and exceeded 33.71 on one day in a hundred. Six days before the cruise it read 33.60. By 5 November it read 34.24, and 13 of the 20 saltiest days in the whole record are from 31 October onward. The CTD at station 93.3 26.7, 11 km from the pier, read 24.34 °C and 34.27 at the surface on 31 October. The salty water reached the pier during the week of the cruise.

3.9 Satellites

Two satellite analyses of sea-surface temperature, each read at every cast’s position on the cast’s day: NOAA’s OISST (Huang et al. 2021; Reynolds et al. 2007) (a 0.25° blend of satellite, ship and buoy data, here in its preliminary near-real-time version, with its own anomaly against 1971–2000) and JPL’s MUR (Chin et al. 2017) (0.01°; the anomaly is NOAA CoastWatch’s product against the MUR climatology of 2003–2014).

code 
d_sat |>
  transmute(
    station = site_key, `cast (UTC)` = sub("T", " ", sub(":\\d\\dZ$", "", cast_time_utc)),
    `CTD, top 3 m (°C)` = round(ctd_t_top3m, 2), `OISST (°C)` = oisst_sst, `OISST anomaly (°C)` = oisst_anom,
    `MUR (°C)` = mur_sst, `MUR anomaly (°C)` = mur_anom) |>
  dt_(caption = "Satellite sea-surface temperature analyses at each cast. An empty cell is a value the data server did not return.")

Across the 36 casts with an OISST value, the analysis follows the CTD closely (correlation 0.96) and reads 0.1 °C warmer on average, as a smoothed quarter-degree product does beside a point measurement in a warm pool with sharp edges.

At the 15 stations of the inner Bight that have one, OISST puts the surface 4.4 to 6.2 °C above its own normal, where the CTD reads 5.4 to 6.9 °C above the CalCOFI normal.

The baselines differ in period and in kind, and the satellite analyses smooth the sharpest part of the warm pool; they agree with the CTD on the size of the event at the surface. The data server returned OISST for 36 and MUR for 0 of the 36 casts when this page was built; the rest are empty in the table.

3.10 Argo floats

code 
at_p <- function(p, t, target) { i <- which.min(abs(p - target)); if (abs(p[i] - target) <= 8) t[i] else NA_real_ }
d_ap <- d_argo |>
  group_by(float = platform_number, cycle = cycle_number, time, latitude, longitude) |>
  summarize(
    `5 m` = at_p(pres, temp, 5), `30 m` = at_p(pres, temp, 30), `50 m` = at_p(pres, temp, 50),
    `75 m` = at_p(pres, temp, 75), `100 m` = at_p(pres, temp, 100), salinity_5m = at_p(pres, psal, 5), .groups = "drop") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    km_all   = list(as.numeric(st_distance(
      st_sfc(st_point(c(longitude, latitude)), crs = 4326),
      st_as_sf(d_casts, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326))) / 1000),
    `nearest station` = d_casts$site_key[which.min(km_all)], `km to it` = round(min(km_all)),
    `CTD there, top 3 m` = d_casts$ctd_t_top3m[which.min(km_all)],
    km_inner = round(min(km_all[d_casts$site_key %in% inner$site_key]))) |>
  ungroup() |> select(-km_all) |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(time), latitude = round(latitude, 2), longitude = round(longitude, 2)) |>
  select(float, cycle, date, latitude, longitude, `5 m`:`100 m`, salinity_5m, `nearest station`, `km to it`, `CTD there, top 3 m`, km_inner) |>
  arrange(date)
km_inner <- min(d_ap$km_inner)
d_ap     <- select(d_ap, -km_inner)
stopifnot(km_inner > 25)   # no float sampled the inner Bight
kable(d_ap, digits = 2, caption = "Argo float profiles in and around the cruise's area, two weeks before it to a week after (temperature in °C at the pressure nearest each depth).")

5 Argo floats (Wong et al. 2020; Argo 2000) surfaced in the area around the cruise. All were over the outer part of the grid or beyond it: none came closer than 32 km to a station, or than 91 km to a station of the inner Bight. They show the offshore structure the cruise found there (surface layers of 18.5–21.0 °C with salinity near 33.5), and so confirm the cool side of the front. The subsurface of the warm pool itself rests on the CTD’s own redundancy: two sensors, two passes, the bottle salinities and the oxygen.

3.11 Verdict

Not an artifact. The normal is the right one (same station, same depth, the cruise’s own month, and the answer barely moves under 7 other definitions). The instrument agrees with itself, with the bottles, with the buoys beside it, with the shore station on Scripps Pier and with the satellite analyses.

4 Where it ranks

The same departure was computed for every cruise, station and 10 m depth bin in the release: the CTD series (143 cruises) and the bottle series (657 cruises), each against its own climatology. Of the 681 cruises, 340 have at least one value with a normal to compare with (why not all).

4.1 Single measurements

code 
d_top <- q("
  SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY anom DESC) AS rank, cruise_key, dataset_key, site_key, depth_bin, depth_m,
         CAST(datetime AS DATE) AS date, v, clim_mean, n_cruises, anom
  FROM cell WHERE anom IS NOT NULL AND cruise_key <> {CRUISE} ORDER BY anom DESC LIMIT 15")
d_top |>
  transmute(
    `rank without 2026` = rank, cruise = cruise_key, series = if_else(dataset_key == "calcofi_bottle", "bottle", "CTD"),
    station = site_key, `depth (m)` = glue("{depth_bin}–{depth_bin + 10}"), date,
    `observed (°C)` = round(v, 2), `normal (°C)` = round(clim_mean, 2), `baseline cruises` = n_cruises, `departure (°C)` = round(anom, 2)) |>
  kable(caption = "The largest single departures in the record outside the fall 2026 cruise.")

Among the 581,071 values with a normal, the 50 largest departures all belong to the fall 2026 cruise, and 98 of the largest 100. 81 of its values exceed the previous record of +7.13 °C.

Two entries in the table are bad data, not warm water, which is the weakness of ranking single values. The January 1994 value is 13.90 °C in the last bin of a cast that reads 6.61 °C ten metres above it. The October 1959 cast at station 93.3 35.0 falls in a perfectly straight line from 19.0 °C at 30 m to 8.0 °C at 400 m (0.74 °C every 25 m): values interpolated across a gap in the source, not measurements. Neither is flagged in the source data. Without them the largest departure before 1993 is +6.06 °C (November 1983).

4.2 Layer averages over the same stations

The fairer comparison averages each cruise over one fixed set of stations, the ones the fall 2026 cruise occupied. A station’s departure profile is averaged over the layer’s 10 m bins (bottle profiles are first interpolated in depth onto those bins), then the stations are averaged. A cruise is ranked when it occupied at least 60 % of those stations in a month that has a normal.

code 
d_l <- d_layer |>
  filter(layer %in% c("0-50 m", "50-200 m")) |>
  mutate(date = date_min + (date_max - date_min) / 2, layer = factor(layer, c("0-50 m", "50-200 m"), c("0–50 m", "50–200 m")))
d_ev <- tibble(
  event = c("1957–59", "1982–83", "1997–98", "2014–16"),
  x0    = as.Date(c("1957-04-01", "1982-07-01", "1997-05-01", "2014-01-01")),
  x1    = as.Date(c("1959-12-31", "1983-12-31", "1998-08-31", "2016-06-30")))
l_top <- d_l |> filter(cruise_key == CRUISE)
l_run <- d_l |> filter(cruise_key != CRUISE) |> group_by(layer) |> slice_max(anom, n = 1, with_ties = F) |> ungroup()

ggplot(d_l, aes(date, anom)) +
  geom_rect(data = d_ev, aes(xmin = x0, xmax = x1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), inherit.aes = F, fill = SAND) +
  geom_text(
    data = mutate(d_ev, layer = factor("0–50 m", levels(d_l$layer))), aes(x = x0 + (x1 - x0) / 2, y = 5.75, label = event),
    inherit.aes = F, colour = MUTED, size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = series, colour = series), size = 1.8, stroke = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = l_top, colour = COL_2026, size = 3.2) +
  geom_text(data = l_top, aes(label = glue("fall 2026  {fs(anom)} °C")), colour = INK, fontface = "bold", size = 3.6, hjust = 1, nudge_x = -500) +
  geom_text(data = l_run, aes(label = glue("{format(date, '%b %Y')}  {fs(anom)}")), colour = INK, size = 3.1, hjust = 1, nudge_x = -400, nudge_y = 0.12) +
  facet_wrap(~ layer, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(bottle = 1, CTD = 16)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(bottle = INK, CTD = COL_NORM)) +
  scale_x_date(breaks = as.Date(paste0(seq(1950, 2020, 10), "-01-01")), date_labels = "%Y", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.03))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = fsa) +
  labs(
    title    = "Every CalCOFI cruise since 1950, averaged over the stations the fall 2026 cruise occupied",
    subtitle = "Mean temperature departure (°C) from the 1993–2013 normal of the cruise's month. Open: bottle casts. Filled: CTD.",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption  = glue("CalCOFI Integrated Database release {VER} (doi:{CAT$doi}). 2026 is preliminary.  calcofi.io")) +
  theme_story() +
  theme(panel.spacing = unit(12, "pt"))
code 
d_layer |>
  filter(layer != "0-200 m") |>
  group_by(layer, series) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(desc(anom)), `of cruises` = n()) |>
  filter(rank <= 6) |> ungroup() |>
  arrange(match(layer, c("surface (0-10 m)", "0-50 m", "50-200 m")), desc(series), rank) |>
  transmute(
    layer, series, rank, `of cruises`, cruise = cruise_key, stations = n_sta, `departure (°C)` = round(anom, 2),
    `warmest station (°C)` = round(anom_max_station, 2), `layer temperature (°C)` = round(temp, 2)) |>
  dt_(caption = "Cruises ranked by layer-mean departure over the fall 2026 stations, by series.")
  • Upper 50 m: +5.10 °C, first of 122 CTD cruises. The previous high is +3.35 °C (2015-11-32OC); the bottle series, 149 cruises back to 1950, has nothing higher.
  • 50–200 m: +2.73 °C, first. The previous high is +1.92 °C (1998-02-31JD, the 1997–98 El Niño). The lead is narrower at depth.
  • The two series agree where they overlap. Over the 102 cruises both cover, their upper-50 m means differ by 0.06 °C on average and never by more than 0.18 °C, so the bottle series stands in fairly for the years before 1993.

4.3 The earlier warm events

code 
d_events <- q("
  WITH ev AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('1957–59', 1957, 1959), ('1982–83 (through 1984)', 1982, 1984), ('1997–98', 1997, 1998),
                                    ('2014–16', 2014, 2016), ('2026', 2026, 2026)) t(event, y0, y1)),
  x AS (SELECT ev.event, l.* FROM cruise_layer l JOIN ev ON l.year BETWEEN ev.y0 AND ev.y1 WHERE l.layer IN ('0-50 m', '50-200 m')),
  m AS (SELECT event, layer, arg_max(cruise_key, anom) AS cruise_m, arg_max(n_sta, anom) AS n_m, max(anom) AS anom_m FROM x WHERE n_sta >= 7 GROUP BY ALL),
  s AS (SELECT event, layer, arg_max(cruise_key, anom_season) AS cruise_s, arg_max(n_sta_season, anom_season) AS n_s, max(anom_season) AS anom_s FROM x WHERE n_sta_season >= 7 GROUP BY ALL)
  SELECT * FROM m FULL JOIN s USING (event, layer) ORDER BY layer, event")
d_events |>
  transmute(
    layer, event, `warmest cruise (monthly normal)` = cruise_m, stations = n_m, `departure (°C)` = round(anom_m, 2),
    `warmest cruise (seasonal normal)` = cruise_s, `stations ` = n_s, `departure from the seasonal normal (°C)` = round(anom_s, 2)) |>
  kable(caption = "Each warm event's warmest cruise over the fall 2026 stations (at least 7 of them occupied).")

The seasonal normal also reaches months that have no monthly normal, such as September and December 1997. The 1982–83 cruises occupied only 7 or 8 of these stations, so the next table compares them, and every other cruise, on exactly the stations they share with fall 2026.

4.4 On the stations two cruises share

code 
d_pair_tbl <- q("
  WITH y AS (
    SELECT layer, 'departure from the monthly normal' AS yardstick, cruise_key, n_month AS n, anom_other AS other, anom_2026 AS y26 FROM paired WHERE n_month >= 10
    UNION ALL SELECT layer, 'departure from the seasonal normal', cruise_key, n_season, season_other, season_2026 FROM paired WHERE n_season >= 10
    UNION ALL SELECT layer, 'temperature itself (no baseline)', cruise_key, n_temp, temp_other, temp_2026 FROM paired WHERE n_temp >= 10)
  SELECT layer, yardstick, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS cruises_compared, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) FILTER (WHERE other >= y26) AS at_or_above_2026,
         arg_min(cruise_key, y26 - other) AS closest_cruise, arg_min(n, y26 - other) AS shared_stations,
         arg_min(other, y26 - other) AS closest_value, arg_min(y26, y26 - other) AS fall_2026, min(y26 - other) AS margin
  FROM y WHERE layer <> '0-200 m' GROUP BY layer, yardstick
  ORDER BY CASE layer WHEN 'surface (0-10 m)' THEN 0 WHEN '0-50 m' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END, yardstick")
d_pair_tbl |>
  transmute(
    layer, yardstick, `cruises compared` = cruises_compared, `at or above fall 2026` = at_or_above_2026,
    `closest cruise` = closest_cruise, `shared stations` = shared_stations, `its value (°C)` = round(closest_value, 2),
    `fall 2026, same stations (°C)` = round(fall_2026, 2), `margin (°C)` = round(margin, 2)) |>
  kable(caption = "Fall 2026 against every other cruise on the stations both occupied (at least 10).")

No cruise in the record equals fall 2026 on shared stations, in any layer, by any of the three yardsticks. The third needs no baseline: it compares the layer’s temperature itself, whatever the month. The margin is about 2 °C in the upper 50 m and 0.4–0.8 °C at 50–200 m. With fewer shared stations the upper 50 m still holds; at depth it gets close: on the 7 offshore stations it shares with the February 1984 cruise, 50–200 m is a tie (1.47 against 1.48 °C).

4.5 Without any baseline

code 
d_warm <- q("
  WITH r AS (SELECT * FROM cell WHERE line BETWEEN 76.7 AND 93.4 AND station <= 120 AND depth_bin < 200 AND v < 35)
  SELECT depth_bin, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS cruises,
         max(v) FILTER (WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE})  AS t_2026,
         max(v) FILTER (WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE}) AS t_before,
         arg_max(cruise_key, v) FILTER (WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE}) AS cruise_before,
         arg_max(site_key, v)   FILTER (WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE}) AS station_before
  FROM r GROUP BY depth_bin ORDER BY depth_bin") |>
  mutate(depth_m = depth_bin + 5, margin = t_2026 - t_before)
z_rec   <- d_warm |> filter(margin > 0) |> pull(depth_bin)
warm_nc <- q("SELECT count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS n, min(cruise_year) AS y0 FROM cell WHERE line BETWEEN 76.7 AND 93.4 AND station <= 120")
stopifnot(all(diff(z_rec) == 10), min(z_rec) == 0)   # one unbroken span from the surface down
w_big   <- d_warm |> slice_max(margin, n = 1)

ggplot(d_warm, aes(y = depth_m)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = \(d) filter(d, margin > 0), aes(xmin = t_before, xmax = t_2026), fill = COL_2026, alpha = 0.12, orientation = "y") +
  geom_path(aes(x = t_before), colour = MUTED, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(x = t_before), colour = MUTED, size = 1.4) +
  geom_path(aes(x = t_2026), colour = COL_2026, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(x = t_2026), colour = COL_2026, size = 1.6) +
  annotate("text", x = 25.4, y = 68, label = "fall 2026", colour = INK, size = 3.4, hjust = 1, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 20.2, y = 24, label = "the warmest before,\nany cruise since 1949", colour = INK, size = 3.2, hjust = 1, lineheight = 0.95) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq(0, 200, 25), expand = expansion(mult = 0.02)) +
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top", breaks = seq(10, 26, 4)) +
  labs(
    title    = glue("The warmest water on record at every depth from the surface to {max(z_rec) + 10} m"),
    subtitle = glue("Highest temperature (°C) in each 10 m bin, {warm_nc$n} cruises on the core grid, any month"),
    x = NULL, y = "Depth (m)") +
  theme_story()

On the core grid (494 cruises since 1949), every depth from the surface to 130 m now has its record on the fall 2026 cruise: by 1.0 °C at the surface (the earlier record, 24.09 °C, was set in August 1983, a summer cruise) and by up to 3.8 °C at 40–50 m. Below 130 m, earlier cruises were warmer.

4.6 Every station ever occupied

The release’s normal exists only where the cruises of 1993–2013 went: the stations of today’s grid. CalCOFI also worked lines far to the south, off Baja California, until the 1980s. None of the rankings above sees them, nor any month that has no normal. One yardstick does: each value against the mean of the other cruises, before fall 2026, of the same series at the same station, calendar month and depth bin, wherever at least five exist. It is a cruder normal than the release’s. Its years differ from station to station, and at today’s stations it includes the warm years since 2014, which makes recent departures read smaller.

code 
# every value against the mean of the OTHER cruises, before fall 2026, of the same series at the same station,
# calendar month and 10 m bin (at least five of them, whatever their years)
invisible(dbExecute(con, glue_sql("
  CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE cell_others AS
  WITH g AS (
    SELECT dataset_key, site_key, cruise_month, depth_bin, count(*) AS n0, sum(v) AS s0
    FROM cell_ok WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE} GROUP BY ALL)
  SELECT c.dataset_key, c.cruise_key, c.cruise_year, c.cruise_month, c.site_key, c.line, c.station, c.depth_bin, c.latitude, c.v, c.anom,
         CASE WHEN c.cruise_key = {CRUISE} THEN g.n0 ELSE g.n0 - 1 END AS n_others,
         CASE WHEN c.cruise_key = {CRUISE} THEN g.s0 / g.n0 ELSE (g.s0 - c.v) / (g.n0 - 1) END AS mean_others
  FROM cell_ok c JOIN g USING (dataset_key, site_key, cruise_month, depth_bin)
  WHERE CASE WHEN c.cruise_key = {CRUISE} THEN g.n0 ELSE g.n0 - 1 END >= 5", .con = con)))
wr <- q("
  SELECT count(*) AS cells, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS cruises, count(*) FILTER (WHERE anom IS NULL) AS cells_no_normal,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE line >= 96) AS cells_south, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) FILTER (WHERE line >= 96) AS cruises_south,
         max(v - mean_others) FILTER (WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE}) AS max_else,
         max(v - mean_others) FILTER (WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE})  AS max_2026
  FROM cell_others")
wr_all <- q("SELECT count(*) AS cells, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS cruises, max(cruise_year) AS y1, count(anom) AS with_normal FROM cell WHERE line >= 96")   # line 96.7 and beyond
stopifnot(wr_all$with_normal == 0)
wr$n_above <- q("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM cell_others WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND v - mean_others > {wr$max_else}")$n
d_wr <- q("
  (SELECT * FROM cell_others WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE}  ORDER BY v - mean_others DESC LIMIT 3)
  UNION ALL
  (SELECT * FROM cell_others WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE} ORDER BY v - mean_others DESC LIMIT 12)") |>
  mutate(dep = v - mean_others) |> arrange(cruise_key != CRUISE, desc(dep))
w65 <- d_wr |> filter(cruise_key != CRUISE) |> slice(1)
w58 <- d_wr |> filter(cruise_key != CRUISE) |> slice(2)
stopifnot(w65$cruise_key == "1965-07-31AX", w58$cruise_key == "1958-10-31PT", wr$max_2026 > wr$max_else)
d_wr |>
  transmute(
    cruise = nb(cruise_key), series = if_else(dataset_key == "calcofi_bottle", "bottle", "CTD"), station = sta(site_key),
    `latitude (°N)` = round(latitude, 1), `depth (m)` = nb(glue("{depth_bin}–{depth_bin + 10}")), `observed (°C)` = round(v, 2),
    `mean of the other cruises (°C)` = round(mean_others, 2), `other cruises` = n_others, `departure (°C)` = round(dep, 2),
    `has a 1993–2013 normal` = if_else(is.na(anom), "no", "yes")) |>
  kable(caption = "Departures from the mean of the other cruises at the same station, calendar month and depth: the three largest of fall 2026, then the twelve largest of every other cruise since 1950.")

Line 96.7 and the lines south of it hold 226,911 values from 322 cruises (the last in 1988), none with a normal, and this yardstick reaches 88,936 of them. In all it covers 772,742 values from 610 cruises, 193,306 of which have no 1993–2013 normal.

By this yardstick too the largest departures in the record are fall 2026’s: +12.0 °C at the most, with 33 of its values above everything else. The largest earlier ones are on the southern lines: +8.8 °C at 20–30 m at station 136.7 23.0, off Baja California at 25.6°N, in July 1965, and +8.5 °C at 50–60 m at station 116.7 30.0 (28.7°N) in October 1958, during the 1957–59 El Niño. The second has the shape of fall 2026 at a smaller size: surface-layer water of 21.6 °C at a depth where that station averages 13.0 °C. The same waters gave the largest value published for the next great El Niño.

5 Trends

5.1 Every November cruise

code 
d_nov <- q("
  SELECT c.cruise_key, r.year, c.site_key, c.latitude AS lat, c.longitude AS lon, c.v, c.anom
  FROM cell c JOIN cruise_ref r USING (cruise_key)
  WHERE c.dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND c.cruise_month = 11 AND c.depth_bin = 0 AND c.anom IS NOT NULL")
d_novm <- d_nov |> group_by(cruise_key, year) |>
  summarize(n = n(), mean = mean(anom), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(label = glue("{year}   {fs(mean)} °C   ({n} stations)"))
d_nov <- d_nov |> left_join(select(d_novm, cruise_key, label), by = "cruise_key") |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, d_novm$label[order(d_novm$year)]))
SFC_MAX <- ceiling(max(abs(d_nov$anom)))

ggplot(d_nov) +
  geom_sf(data = land, fill = SAND, colour = STONE, linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_point(aes(lon, lat, fill = anom), shape = 21, size = 1.9, colour = MUTED, stroke = 0.15) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, ncol = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = cmocean("balance")(256), limits = c(-SFC_MAX, SFC_MAX), breaks = seq(-8, 8, 4), labels = fsa,
    name = "°C from the November normal",
    guide = guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal", title.position = "top", barwidth = unit(170, "pt"), barheight = unit(8, "pt"), frame.colour = STONE)) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-124.9, -116.6), ylim = c(29.6, 35.3), expand = F) +
  labs(
    title    = "Twenty Novembers at the sea surface",
    subtitle = "Temperature departure (°C) at each station, 0–10 m. One colour scale for every year.",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption  = glue("CalCOFI CTD; CalCOFI Integrated Database release {VER} (doi:{CAT$doi}). Preliminary from 2021.  calcofi.io")) +
  theme_story(10) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#eaf1f6", colour = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8.2), legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_text(size = 9), legend.text = element_text(size = 8.5, colour = MUTED),
    panel.spacing = unit(6, "pt"))

The years after the baseline do not warm steadily. The surface was warm in 2014 and 2015 (+2.0 and +2.7 °C), near normal in 2021 and 2022, below normal in 2024 (−1.2 °C), and then +4.3 °C in 2026, on a cruise that covered only the southern lines.

code 
# each November cruise at the surface: over its own stations, and over the stations the fall 2026 cruise occupied
d_novt <- q("
  WITH own AS (
    SELECT cruise_key, count(*) AS n_surface, count(anom) AS n_normal, avg(anom) AS anom_own
    FROM cell WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND cruise_month = 11 AND depth_bin = 0 GROUP BY cruise_key)
  SELECT r.year, o.cruise_key, r.ship_name, r.ctd_stage, o.n_surface, o.n_normal, o.anom_own, l.n_sta AS n_2026, l.anom AS anom_2026
  FROM own o JOIN cruise_ref r USING (cruise_key)
  LEFT JOIN cruise_layer l ON l.cruise_key = o.cruise_key AND l.dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND l.layer = 'surface (0-10 m)'
  ORDER BY r.year")
nov15 <- d_novt |> filter(year == 2015)
stopifnot(nov15$anom_2026 == max(d_novt$anom_2026[d_novt$year < 2026]))
d_novt |>
  transmute(
    year, cruise = nb(cruise_key), ship = str_to_title(ship_name), `stations with a surface value` = n_surface, `with a normal` = n_normal,
    `mean over its own stations (°C)` = round(anom_own, 2), `of the fall 2026 stations` = n_2026,
    `mean over those (°C)` = round(anom_2026, 2), `data stage` = ctd_stage) |>
  kable(caption = "Every November cruise at the sea surface (0–10 m): its mean departure over its own stations, and over the stations the fall 2026 cruise occupied.")

A cruise’s own stations change from year to year, so the last columns put every November on the stations of the fall 2026 cruise; these are the bars along the bottom of the animation. On that footing the previous high is +3.2 °C in 2015 (32 of the 35 stations), against +4.3 °C in 2026.

5.2 Through 2026

code 
d_26 <- q("
  SELECT l.cruise_key, c.date_min, c.date_max, l.layer, l.anom, l.n_sta
  FROM cruise_layer l JOIN cruise_ref c USING (cruise_key)
  WHERE l.year = 2026 AND l.dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND l.layer IN ('surface (0-10 m)', '0-50 m', '50-200 m')") |>
  mutate(anom = round(anom, 2)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = layer, values_from = c(anom, n_sta)) |>
  arrange(date_min)
d_26 |>
  transmute(
    cruise = cruise_key, dates = glue("{trimws(format(date_min, '%e %b'))} – {trimws(format(date_max, '%e %b'))}"),
    `surface (°C)` = `anom_surface (0-10 m)`, `0–50 m (°C)` = `anom_0-50 m`, `50–200 m (°C)` = `anom_50-200 m`,
    `stations (0–50 m)` = `n_sta_0-50 m`) |>
  kable(caption = "The four cruises of 2026: mean departure over the stations the fall cruise occupied, each against its own month's normal.")

The same stations were already about 2 °C warm in the upper 50 m in January and April 2026 and 1.5 °C warm in July, with little signal below 50 m. Between July and November the upper 50 m gained a further 3.6 °C of departure and the layer beneath it 2.1 °C. The buoy records say the inshore surface had been at 22 to 25 °C since at least late September.

5.3 The long record

code 
d_tr <- d_layer |>
  filter(layer == "0-50 m", cruise_key != CRUISE) |>
  mutate(t = as.numeric(date_min + (date_max - date_min) / 2 - as.Date("1990-01-01")) / 3652.5)   # decades from 1990
fit_b <- lm(anom ~ t, data = filter(d_tr, series == "bottle"))
fit_c <- lm(anom ~ t, data = filter(d_tr, series == "CTD"))
tr <- list(
  b = coef(summary(fit_b))["t", ], c = coef(summary(fit_c))["t", ],
  sd_b = sd(resid(fit_b)), sd_all = sd(d_tr$anom),
  yrs_b = range(filter(d_tr, series == "bottle")$year), yrs_c = range(filter(d_tr, series == "CTD")$year))

Over these stations the upper 50 m has warmed slowly: a straight-line fit to the bottle series (1950–2021, 149 cruises) rises by 0.11 °C per decade (standard error 0.04), and the CTD series (1993–2026, without the fall 2026 cruise) by 0.24 °C per decade (standard error 0.07). Cruises are unevenly spaced and successive cruises are not independent, so these standard errors are too small; the slopes are a description, not a test.

The fall 2026 departure is not a point on that line. Cruise-to-cruise scatter over the whole record has a standard deviation of 0.80 °C, so +5.1 °C is 6 standard deviations from normal, and 1.7 °C beyond anything else in it.

6 The water mass

code 
d_ts <- q("
  SELECT t.site_key, t.depth_m, t.value AS temp, s.value AS sal
  FROM cast_1m t JOIN cast_1m s USING (sample_key, depth_m)
  WHERE t.measurement_type = 'temperature_ave' AND s.measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr'
    AND t.direction = 'd' AND t.measurement_qual IS NULL AND s.measurement_qual IS NULL AND t.depth_m <= 200") |>
  mutate(group = if_else(site_key %in% inner$site_key, "inner Bight", "seaward"))
# the normal curve is the BOTTLE series' (temperature and salinity at the bottle depths): the CTD salinity normal at
# this station is inflated at 90-120 m by one unflagged cast (see the note under the figure)
d_tsn <- q("
  SELECT t.depth_bin, t.clim_mean AS temp, s.clim_mean AS sal
  FROM climatology t JOIN climatology s USING (dataset_key, site_key, month, depth_bin)
  WHERE t.measurement_type = 'temperature' AND s.measurement_type = 'salinity' AND t.dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle'
    AND t.site_key = {k$top_site} AND t.month = 11 AND t.depth_bin <= 200 AND t.clim_mean IS NOT NULL AND s.clim_mean IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY t.depth_bin")
d_bad <- q("
  SELECT c.depth_bin, c.clim_mean AS ctd_normal, c.clim_sd, b.clim_mean AS bottle_normal,
         (SELECT max(value) FROM obs_env o WHERE o.measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr' AND o.site_key = c.site_key
            AND o.cruise_key = '2007-11-32NM' AND o.depth_bin = c.depth_bin) AS cast_2007
  FROM climatology c LEFT JOIN climatology b
    ON b.measurement_type = 'salinity' AND b.dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle' AND b.site_key = c.site_key AND b.month = c.month AND b.depth_bin = c.depth_bin
  WHERE c.measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr' AND c.dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND c.site_key = {k$top_site} AND c.month = 11
    AND c.depth_bin BETWEEN 90 AND 120 ORDER BY c.depth_bin")
# lines of equal density (TEOS-10, at the sea surface)
d_sig <- expand_grid(sal = seq(32.7, 34.8, 0.02), temp = seq(8, 26.5, 0.1)) |>
  mutate(sigma = gsw_sigma0(gsw_SA_from_SP(sal, 0, -118, 33), gsw_CT_from_t(gsw_SA_from_SP(sal, 0, -118, 33), temp, 0)))
d_sig_lab <- d_sig |> filter(abs(temp - 26.2) < 0.01) |> mutate(s_ = round(sigma * 2) / 2) |>
  filter(s_ %in% c(22, 23), abs(sigma - s_) < 0.008) |> group_by(s_) |> slice(1)

ggplot(d_ts, aes(sal, temp)) +
  geom_contour(data = d_sig, aes(z = sigma), breaks = seq(21, 27, 0.5), colour = STONE, linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(data = d_sig_lab, aes(label = s_), colour = MUTED, size = 2.8, vjust = -0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = group), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_path(data = d_tsn, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = filter(d_tsn, depth_bin %in% c(0, 50, 100, 200)), colour = INK, size = 1.9) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = filter(d_tsn, depth_bin %in% c(0, 50, 100, 200)), aes(label = glue("{depth_bin} m")), colour = INK, size = 2.9,
    bg.color = "white", bg.r = 0.18, nudge_x = -0.07, direction = "y", segment.colour = NA, seed = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 34.44, y = 24.45, label = "inner Bight,\nsurface to 55 m", colour = INK, size = 3.1, lineheight = 0.9, hjust = 0, vjust = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 33.05, y = 21.2, label = "seaward stations", colour = INK, size = 3.1, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 34.14, y = 13.6, label = "November normal,\nstation 93.3 30.0\n(bottle series)", colour = INK, size = 3.1, lineheight = 0.9, hjust = 0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("inner Bight" = COL_2026, seaward = COL_NORM)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(33, 34.5, 0.5), limits = c(32.85, 34.72), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(10, 26, 4), limits = c(8, 26.6), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title    = "The warm layer is saltier than anything normally found here",
    subtitle = "Temperature (°C) against salinity, fall 2026 down casts, surface to 200 m",
    x = "Salinity", y = NULL) +
  theme_story()

Temperature alone cannot say where water came from; temperature and salinity together can. The seaward stations plot where the California Current always does: fresh at the surface (33.3–33.6 in the top 40 m) and saltier with depth. The normal profile at the record station does the same (33.33–33.48 in the top 40 m, 34.10 at 200 m). Across the inner Bight the top 40 m is 33.8 to 34.4, and at stations 28 and 30 the warm layer (34.43–34.48) is saltier than any water the normal column holds down to 200 m, while lying at the surface, where the normal is freshest. Local heating moves water straight up on this diagram; it cannot move it to the right.

The quantity of heat makes the same point. Through the upper 200 m at station 093.3 028.0 the water column holds about 6.0 GJ per square metre more heat than normal (2.6 GJ m⁻² on average over the 27 stations sampled to 200 m). At a net surface heating of 100 W m⁻², a generous figure chosen only for scale, the atmosphere would need about 690 days to supply it. Both the salt and the heat say this water was carried in, not warmed where it lies. The Scripps Pier record shows it arriving at the coast: salinity there rose by 0.6 within about ten days.

6.1 Warm and salty, or only warm?

Salinity also separates this event from the last one. The table puts every cruise on one footing: its mean departure through the upper 50 m at the stations of the inner Bight, in temperature and in salinity, against the bottle series’ normals. Earlier cruises are their bottle casts; fall 2026 is its CTD, whose salinity matches the bottles drawn on board.

code 
ts59 <- d_tsx |> filter(year %in% 1957:1959) |> slice_max(t_anom, n = 1)
d_tsx |>
  mutate(s_rank = rank(-s_anom)) |>
  slice_max(t_anom, n = 8) |>
  transmute(
    cruise = nb(cruise_key), stations = n_s, `temperature (°C)` = round(t_anom, 2), `salinity` = round(s_anom, 2),
    `salinity, station by station` = glue("{fs(s_min, 2)} to {fs(s_max, 2)}"), `salinity rank` = s_rank) |>
  kable(caption = glue("The eight warmest cruises in the inner Southern California Bight, upper 50 m: mean departure of temperature and of salinity from the bottle series' normals, and where the salinity departure ranks among the {nrow(d_tsx)} cruises with at least 8 of these stations."))

The warm water of 2014–15 was warm only. November 2015 stands +3.9 °C above normal and 0.00 in salinity; the State of the California Current report of the time found the upper ocean “unusually fresh during 2015 in most regions off southern California” (McClatchie et al. 2016). The water of the 1997–98 El Niño was warm and salty: +2.6 °C and +0.38 in February 1998, when the inshore countercurrent carried “a salinity anomaly as much as +0.5” (Lynn et al. 1998). The 1957–59 warm period has the same sign: about 0.2 in the mixed layer of January 1958 (Reid 1960), and +0.19 here in August 1959. The 1982–83 El Niño differed again: its subsurface water was fresher than normal (Simpson 1984).

Fall 2026 is of the salty kind and beyond it: +0.65, the highest of the 155 cruises, where the cruise-to-cruise standard deviation is 0.12. By its salt this water resembles what the 1997 El Niño brought to Baja California, 0.8 above normal on line 120 in October 1997 (Lynn et al. 1998), more than anything measured before off Southern California.

6.2 Displaced water, or different water?

A deep warm layer pushes everything beneath it down, and that alone makes large departures at a fixed depth: the water at 100 m is warm partly because it is water that normally sits at 30 m. Following surfaces of equal density separates the two effects: how far each surface moved, and whether the water on it changed. This is done here at the record station from the one-metre down casts: fall 2026, and the casts of the 6 November cruises behind its normal.

code 
# every one-metre down cast at the record station: the baseline's November cruises and fall 2026
d_iso <- q("
  WITH f AS (SELECT * FROM obs_ctd_full_base UNION ALL BY NAME SELECT * FROM obs_ctd_full)
  SELECT f.cruise_key, f.depth_min_m AS depth_m,
         max(f.measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE f.measurement_type = 'temperature_ave')   AS temp,
         max(f.measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE f.measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr') AS sal
  FROM f JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
  WHERE s.site_key = {k$top_site} AND right(f.sample_key, 1) = 'd' AND f.measurement_qual IS NULL
    AND f.measurement_type IN ('temperature_ave', 'salinity_ave_corr')
  GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY f.cruise_key, depth_m") |>
  filter(!is.na(temp), !is.na(sal)) |>
  mutate(
    sa    = gsw_SA_from_SP(sal, depth_m, top$longitude, top$latitude),
    sigma = gsw_sigma0(sa, gsw_CT_from_t(sa, temp, depth_m)),          # potential density anomaly, kg m-3 (TEOS-10)
    when  = if_else(cruise_key == CRUISE, "fall 2026", "normal"))

# depth, temperature and salinity where a cast first reaches each density (NA where the cast never holds it)
SIG <- seq(24.5, 26.5, 0.5)
on_sigma <- function(d, ...) {
  d <- arrange(d, depth_m) |> mutate(sig_m = cummax(sigma))            # a stable column: density never falls with depth
  tibble(sigma = SIG) |> mutate(
    depth = approx(d$sig_m, d$depth_m, xout = sigma, ties = min, rule = 1)$y,
    temp  = approx(d$depth_m, d$temp, xout = depth)$y,
    sal   = approx(d$depth_m, d$sal,  xout = depth)$y)}
d_on  <- d_iso |> group_by(cruise_key, when) |> group_modify(on_sigma) |> ungroup()
d_onn <- d_on |> filter(when == "normal") |> group_by(sigma) |>
  summarize(n = sum(!is.na(depth)), across(c(depth, temp, sal), list(mean = \(x) mean(x, na.rm = T), sd = \(x) sd(x, na.rm = T))), .groups = "drop")
d_on26 <- d_on |> filter(when == "fall 2026") |> select(sigma, depth_26 = depth, temp_26 = temp, sal_26 = sal)
d_surf <- left_join(d_onn, d_on26, by = "sigma") |> filter(n == nrow(b_in), !is.na(depth_26))

d_surf |>
  transmute(
    `density surface (σθ, kg m⁻³)` = f1(sigma),
    `normal depth (m)` = glue("{round(depth_mean)} ± {round(depth_sd)}"), `depth in 2026 (m)` = round(depth_26),
    `deeper by (m)` = round(depth_26 - depth_mean),
    `normal temperature (°C)` = glue("{f1(temp_mean, 2)} ± {f1(temp_sd, 2)}"), `in 2026 (°C)` = round(temp_26, 2),
    `warmer by (°C)` = round(temp_26 - temp_mean, 2),
    `normal salinity` = glue("{f1(sal_mean, 2)} ± {f1(sal_sd, 2)}"), `in 2026` = round(sal_26, 2), `saltier by` = round(sal_26 - sal_mean, 2)) |>
  kable(align = "r", caption = glue("Station 93.3 30.0 on surfaces of equal density: fall 2026 beside the mean (± 1 standard deviation) of the {nrow(b_in)} November baseline casts."))

Two things stand out.

The upper 80 m is not normal water pushed down. In the baseline casts the sea surface has a density of 24.09 kg m⁻³ on average, and 23.97 in the lightest of them. In fall 2026 the surface was 22.92, and the water did not become as dense as the lightest baseline surface until 80 m (as dense as the average one until 92 m). Everything above that depth is lighter than any water those six casts contain. It has no counterpart in the normal column to have been displaced from: it is water that is not normally there.

Beneath it, the density surfaces lay 79 to 113 m deeper than normal, and the water on them had changed as well. On the same surfaces it was 0.3 to 1.0 °C warmer and 0.05 to 0.29 saltier than the baseline mean, 1 to 3 standard deviations of the six casts. At 150 m, for example, the departure of +2.9 °C splits into +2.0 °C from displacement (the water there has the density the normal column holds at 40 m) and +0.9 °C from the water itself being warmer on that surface.

code 
# the same on every station of the cruise: the baseline is the median of the six cruises' down casts at the station
d_ia <- q("
  WITH f AS (SELECT * FROM obs_ctd_full_base UNION ALL BY NAME SELECT * FROM obs_ctd_full)
  SELECT f.cruise_key, s.site_key, f.depth_min_m AS depth_m,
         max(f.measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE f.measurement_type = 'temperature_ave')   AS temp,
         max(f.measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE f.measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr') AS sal
  FROM f JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
  WHERE right(f.sample_key, 1) = 'd' AND f.measurement_qual IS NULL AND f.depth_min_m <= 450
    AND f.measurement_type IN ('temperature_ave', 'salinity_ave_corr') AND s.site_key IN ({unique(d_sta$site_key)*})
  GROUP BY ALL") |>
  filter(!is.na(temp), !is.na(sal)) |>
  mutate(
    sa    = gsw_SA_from_SP(sal, depth_m, -119, 33),
    sigma = gsw_sigma0(sa, gsw_CT_from_t(sa, temp, depth_m)),
    when  = if_else(cruise_key == CRUISE, "fall 2026", "normal"))
SIG_ALL <- c(25.5, 26)
d_oa <- d_ia |> group_by(site_key, cruise_key, when) |>
  group_modify(\(d, ...) on_sigma(d) |> filter(sigma %in% SIG_ALL)) |> ungroup()
d_dz <- d_oa |> filter(when == "normal") |> group_by(site_key, sigma) |>
  summarize(n = sum(!is.na(depth)), depth_n = median(depth, na.rm = T), temp_n = median(temp, na.rm = T), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n >= 4) |>
  inner_join(d_oa |> filter(when == "fall 2026", !is.na(depth)) |> select(site_key, sigma, depth_26 = depth, temp_26 = temp), by = c("site_key", "sigma")) |>
