  mutate(group = if_else(site_key %in% inner$site_key, "inner Bight", "seaward"), dz = depth_26 - depth_n, dt = temp_26 - temp_n)
d_dz |>
  group_by(`density surface (σθ)` = f1(sigma), stations = group) |>
  summarize(
    `stations with a baseline` = n(), `median deeper by (m)` = round(median(dz)), `range (m)` = glue("{round(min(dz))} to {round(max(dz))}"),
    `median warmer on the surface (°C)` = round(median(dt), 2), .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(align = "r", caption = "Every station of the cruise deep enough to hold the surface: how far two density surfaces lay below their baseline depth (the median of the six November baseline casts at the station), and the temperature change on them.")

The displacement is not confined to the record station. Across the cruise the same surfaces lay deeper than their baseline at 49 of 54 station-surface pairs: by a median of 84 m in the inner Bight and 26 m at the seaward stations.

So the depressed pycnocline accounts for most of the departure below about 80 m, as expected of a deep warm layer, and the layer itself is a different water mass. A baseline on density surfaces for every station, built from the one-metre casts of the whole baseline period, would make this routine; here it is done by hand, from six cruises.

NoteA flaw in the salinity normal, found while drawing this figure

The diagram draws the normal from the bottle series because the CTD salinity normal at this station is wrong at 90–130 m: 33.89–34.12 where the bottles give 33.72–33.85. One cast of the November 2007 cruise carries unflagged salinities up to 35.34 there, which no water off California reaches, and they enter the mean. It does not touch the temperature normal, nor the salinity normal of the warm layer above 60 m, whose standard deviation is about 0.11. It is recorded here because this analysis is where it surfaced.

7 The event in context

7.1 What the agencies were reporting in fall 2026

These are other institutions’ statements, quoted as published and read on 12–13 November 2026. They are context for the measurements above, not part of them.

  • A strong El Niño is in progress. NOAA’s Climate Prediction Center, in its ENSO Diagnostic Discussion of 12 November 2026 (NOAA Climate Prediction Center 2026), keeps an El Niño Advisory in force: “El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027”. Its Niño-3.4 index for October was +2.5 °C. That is a relative index (the tropical mean is subtracted (Oldenborgh et al. 2021; L’Heureux et al. 2024)), which NOAA has used officially since February 2026, so it is not comparable with the Niño-3.4 values quoted for earlier events without saying which index is meant. At the equator NOAA reports “a deeper-than-average thermocline and anomalies exceeding +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean”: large departures at thermocline depth are how this event looks at its source as well.
  • A marine heatwave was already there. NOAA Fisheries’ California Current Marine Heatwave Tracker (updated 30 October 2026) (NOAA Integrated Ecosystem Assessment 2026) has followed a heatwave off California, NEP25A, since May 2025, and says of the recent warming: “Although the current MHW off California preceded the El Niño, we now infer that we are seeing additional warming due to El Niño, primarily through the arrival of Kelvin waves, which act to further deepen the surface mixed layer, reduce upwelling, and therefore lead to surface layer warming. It is unclear if we can separate the warming that was already in place in California from the additional warming due to the El Niño-forced Kelvin waves.”
  • Scripps Pier’s century-long record. The Shore Stations Program has measured the sea surface at the pier by hand every day since 1916. Its plot for 2026 (Shore Stations Program, Scripps Institution of Oceanography 2026) gives 24.0 °C for 12 November, counts 74 daily record highs in 2026 so far, and marks the days of early November as records for their dates. (This is the long manual record; the automated station above is a separate instrument on the same pier.)
  • Gliders. Scripps’s underwater gliders have repeated CalCOFI line 90 for twenty years. The group’s El Niño page (Instrument Development Group, Scripps Institution of Oceanography 2026) says of that line: “The warm water anomaly is now extending the deepest we’ve seen in 20 years of monitoring.”
  • A published anomaly at thermocline depth, farther north. In Monterey Bay, MBARI reported on 29 October 2026 (Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute 2026) that the temperature at 60 m “reached 18.18 degrees Celsius (64.72 degrees Fahrenheit), surpassing the time series record high set on November 19, 1997”, with temperatures “more than seven degrees centigrade over the long-term average”. That is the same kind of number as the one on this page, a departure at the depth of the thermocline, from an independent mooring about 600 km to the north-west, and a little over half as large.

Read together: the water CalCOFI measured arrived on top of a marine heatwave that had been in place for a year and a half, during a strong El Niño. The measurements on this page do not separate the two, and NOAA says it cannot yet either.

7.2 The glider index, not yet at its record in September

code 
gl_last <- slice_tail(d_gl, n = 1)
gl_top  <- slice_max(d_gl, scti, n = 1)
gl_rank <- sum(d_gl$scti > gl_last$scti) + 1
# CalCOFI's own casts on that stretch of line 90, at 50-60 m: the cruises whose six stations all have a normal
d_l90 <- q("
  SELECT cruise_key, count(*) AS n, avg(anom) AS anom, string_agg(CAST(CAST(station AS INTEGER) AS VARCHAR), ' ' ORDER BY station) AS stations
  FROM cell WHERE dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND line = 90 AND station BETWEEN 27 AND 54 AND depth_bin = 50 AND anom IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY cruise_key")
l90 <- function(cruise) d_l90 |> filter(cruise_key == cruise)
stopifnot(l90(CRUISE)$stations == l90("2015-11-32OC")$stations, l90(CRUISE)$n == 6, gl_top$date > as.Date("2015-10-01"), gl_top$date < as.Date("2016-02-01"))

ggplot(d_gl, aes(date, scti)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = INK, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(colour = COL_NORM, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = gl_top, colour = COL_2015, size = 2.6) +
  geom_point(data = gl_last, colour = COL_2026, size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(data = gl_top, aes(label = glue("{format(date, '%b %Y')}  {fs(scti)} °C")), colour = INK, size = 3.3, hjust = 1, nudge_x = -200, nudge_y = 0.1) +
  geom_text(data = gl_last, aes(label = glue("{format(date, '%b %Y')}  {fs(scti)} °C")), colour = INK, fontface = "bold", size = 3.3, hjust = 1, nudge_x = -200) +
  scale_x_date(breaks = as.Date(paste0(seq(2008, 2026, 2), "-01-01")), date_labels = "%Y", expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.03))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = fsa) +
  labs(
    title    = "At 50 m on line 90, the gliders' three-month mean was climbing toward its 2015 record",
    subtitle = "Southern California Temperature Index (°C): coast to 200 km offshore, three-month running mean",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption  = "Scripps Instrument Development Group, California Underwater Glider Network (doi:10.21238/S8SPRAY7292).") +
  theme_story()

The glider group publishes one number for line 90, the Southern California Temperature Index: “the interannual temperature anomaly at 50m depth along the coastal section of Line 90 (coast to 200-km offshore) with a 3-month running mean applied” (Rudnick et al. 2016). Its latest value, centred on September 2026, is +2.8 °C, the third highest of 237 months since 2007; the record is +3.3 °C, centred on December 2015. The index ends six weeks before the cruise and averages three months, so it does not yet cover what the ship found, and it neither confirms nor contradicts it. CalCOFI’s own casts on that stretch of the line say what to expect: its six stations averaged +8.7 °C at 50–60 m on the fall 2026 cruise, and +3.1 °C in November 2015, when the index centred on that month was +3.3 °C. The index for November 2026 will be the independent check on a record at that depth.

7.3 How large earlier warm events were

What their observers published about the earlier warm events, with the baseline each used. No study uses the 1993–2013 normal of this page, and most report averages over a cruise, a section or a month, not single stations, so sizes compare only loosely. Words in quotation marks are the authors’.

code 
# published values, each read in the source named (or in its abstract, where the last column says so)
d_lit <- read_csv(file.path(DIR_DATA, "literature_ranges.csv"))
d_lit |>
  transmute(
    event, `where and what` = what, reported, `against` = baseline,
    source = glue("[@{key}]{if_else(read == 'abstract', ' (abstract)', '')}")) |>
  kable(caption = "Temperature departures published for earlier warm events off Southern California and Baja California, each against its own baseline.")

Three things follow from setting these beside the release.

The ranking sees the earlier events at the sizes their observers reported. The largest value in the table for today’s grid is the “greater than 6°” that Hayward et al. (1999) found in the thermocline at station 90.60 in December 1997. That cruise is in the release (1997-12-32QU, 9 stations). Its largest value here is +6.5 °C, at station 90.0 53.0, 80–90 m, against the seasonal normal because December has no monthly one. At station 90.60 itself the release gives +5.4 °C against that normal, which is not the paper’s 1950–92 baseline, and +6.2 °C against the mean of the other December cruises. For 1982–83 the release’s largest is +6.1 °C (1983-11-31JD, station 90.0 60.0, 50–60 m), where McLain et al. (1985) give “+5° to +6°C at 100 m”. For November 2015 the upper 50 m averages +3.4 °C over the fall 2026 stations, where glider sections gave departures “frequently greater than 3 °C” for 10–100 m against 2007–2013 (Ren and Rudnick 2021). One cruise the literature describes is not in the release: NOAA ship McArthur, 17–22 November 1997, the first of the extra cruises added that winter (Lynn et al. 1998), on which station 90.30 showed thermocline departures “greater than 4°” (Hayward et al. 1999).

The largest published value is from Baja California, and it is smaller. On the first cruise of the Mexican IMECOCAL programme, in early October 1997, the water 30 to 40 m down off Punta Eugenia (line 120) was 8 °C above the 1950–78 October mean and 0.8 saltier (Lynn et al. 1998), “up to 8.7 °C” at 50 m (Durazo and Baumgartner 2002). That cruise is not in the CalCOFI database. CalCOFI’s own casts on those lines in the 1957–59 El Niño are, and the whole-record ranking finds the same size there, +8.5 °C in October 1958. It is the nearest published analogue to fall 2026: a warm, salty surface layer lying where the thermocline normally is, in the autumn of a very strong El Niño. Fall 2026 found that structure off San Diego, and larger.

At the sea surface fall 2026 is not beyond what 2014–16 produced; beneath it, it is. The largest departures published for 2014–16 near the surface off Southern California are about 6 °C: 6.2 °C in satellite sea-surface temperature (Gentemann et al. 2017) and 5.8 °C in daily bottom temperature at 7–10 m in the Santa Barbara Channel (Reed et al. 2016). That is the size of the 5 to 8 °C at the inner-Bight stations of this cruise. The difference is underneath. In 2015 the warming was “confined to the surface layer (upper ~50 m)” (Leising et al. 2015) and reached 0.5 to 1.5 °C at 100 m (McClatchie et al. 2016); in fall 2026 the 50–200 m layer averages +2.7 °C over 27 stations. That is why the record on this page rests on the values below the surface and on the layer averages, not on the sea surface.

7.4 Marine heatwaves, and why the largest numbers are below the surface

A marine heatwave has a standard definition: “a prolonged discrete anomalously warm water event” that “lasts for five or more days, with temperatures warmer than the 90th percentile based on a 30-year historical baseline period” (Hobday et al. 2016), graded from moderate to extreme by how many times the local gap between the mean and that percentile is exceeded (Hobday et al. 2018). It is defined on daily sea-surface temperature, which a cruise cannot supply. NOAA’s tracker identifies heatwaves in satellite sea-surface temperature by a rule of its own, on strength and area (NOAA Integrated Ecosystem Assessment 2026); that is the heatwave named above.

By that yardstick the well-known events are a few degrees. The regional mean on the peak day of the ten examples Hobday et al. (2018) tabulate runs from 1.92 to 5.10 °C against 1983–2012; the largest is the Santa Barbara Channel in October 2015, and the Northeast Pacific “Blob” is 2.56 °C. Eight prominent events reviewed by Smale et al. (2019) had maximum intensities of “3.5 to 9.5°C above climatological SST”. The +5.1 °C mean of the upper 50 m over 32 stations is at the top of the first range, and it is a 50 m layer, not a skin temperature.

Below the surface the numbers are larger, and the literature says why: “These subsurface anomalies are often larger than surface anomalies, due to the movement of the strong vertical temperature gradients around the thermocline” (Capotondi et al. 2024). At moorings in the tropical western Pacific the mean intensity of subsurface heatwaves “shows a peak of about 5.2 °C at 150 m, and the maximal mean intensity reaches 8.9 °C” (Hu et al. 2021), and a model study finds that deep-reaching events “tend to reach deepest along the west coasts of the Americas, especially in the California Current System” (Köhn et al. 2024). No published temperature departure found in the search behind this page, for California or anywhere else, reaches 12.8 °C. That is weak evidence by itself, because papers report averages far more often than single stations. The evidence for the record is the ranking above.

7.5 How El Niño warms these waters

The review by Jacox et al. (2017) names three routes. The measurements on this page bear on two of them.

  • Waves along the coast. “During an El Niño, these waves tend to deepen the pycnocline and nutricline” (Jacox et al. 2017): coastally trapped waves that travel poleward from the equator. Earlier events deepened the thermocline off Southern California by tens of metres in cruise and winter means: the mixed layer by 10 to 30 m in January 1958 (Reid 1960), the 14 °C isotherm off San Diego by more than 40 m in winter 1982–83, and the thermocline along the coast “by 50 to 100 m” (McLain et al. 1985). At the record station in fall 2026 the density surfaces lay 79 to 113 m below their November depths (above).
  • Water from the south. “anomalous advection of surface waters from the south, as observed during the 1997-98 El Niño”, which “may amplify surface warming and water column stratification” (Jacox et al. 2017). Its mark is salt, and fall 2026 is the saltiest cruise on record in the inner Bight.
  • Winds. A changed atmosphere over the North Pacific weakens the winds that drive upwelling. A cruise does not measure this.

El Niños differ, and the same literature says so. The subsurface water of 1982–83 was fresher than normal, not saltier (Simpson 1984). Gliders in the 2009–10 event found isopycnals “abnormally deep” but “no anomalous water masses in the region” (Todd et al. 2011). In 2015–16 the effects on the California Current were “weaker than expected based on tropical sea surface temperature anomalies” (Jacox et al. 2016). And the background has moved: “An overall warming trend of 1.3°C in the ocean surface, a deepening in the depth of the mean thermocline (18 m)” between 1950 and 1999 (Di Lorenzo et al. 2005), which a fixed 1993–2013 normal folds into any recent departure.

8 What this does and does not show

code 
d_cov <- q("
  SELECT CASE dataset_key WHEN 'calcofi_bottle' THEN 'bottle' ELSE 'CTD' END AS series, CAST((cruise_year // 10) * 10 AS INTEGER) || 's' AS decade,
         count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS cruises, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) FILTER (WHERE anom IS NOT NULL) AS with_monthly_normal,
         count(DISTINCT cruise_key) FILTER (WHERE anom_season IS NOT NULL) AS with_seasonal_normal,
         CAST(round(100.0 * count(anom) / count(*)) AS INTEGER) AS pct_values_with_monthly_normal
  FROM cell GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY series DESC, decade")
n_site <- q("SELECT count(DISTINCT site_key) AS n, min(line) AS l0, max(line) AS l1 FROM cell WHERE anom IS NOT NULL")
months <- q("SELECT DISTINCT cruise_month AS m FROM cell WHERE anom IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1")$m
kable(d_cov, col.names = c("series", "decade", "cruises", "with a monthly normal", "with a seasonal normal", "% of values with a monthly normal"),
      caption = "How much of the record has a normal to compare with.")
  • “The record” is the part of the record with a baseline. A normal exists for 81 stations of the present grid (lines 66.7 to 93.4) and for the months with at least five cruises in 1993–2013: January, February, April, July, August, October, November. Earlier decades sampled other months and other stations far more often. “The largest on record” means the largest among 340 of 681 cruises. The baseline-free comparisons (shared stations, record temperatures) and the yardstick that reaches every station do not have this limit and give the same answer.
  • The baseline is thin. 6 to 8 November cruises per bin on line 93.3. The baseline table bounds what that can change: the peak departure stays between 11.4 and 13.0 °C.
  • Coverage. 36 stations in 8 days, where a full cruise occupies 65 to 75. The layer averages are over those stations only; a whole-grid average would be lower and cannot be computed for this cruise.
  • Preliminary. The casts are one-metre averages processed at sea. Two sensors agreeing within 0.006 °C and bottle salinities agreeing within 0.002 leave little for final calibration to change.
  • Single values or layer averages. A ranking of single values rewards the thermocline, where a displaced layer makes the largest numbers, and it is where bad values in old data surface. The layer average over fixed stations is the fairer claim. Both rank fall 2026 first.
  • Peaks between cruises. CalCOFI samples four times a year. The peak of the 1997–98 El Niño on line 90 was caught because extra cruises were added that winter (Lynn et al. 1998), and one of them is not in the release (above). An earlier event’s largest departure may have fallen between cruises; so may this one’s.
  • A defect in the published one-metre table does not reach this page. In releases v2026.11.05 and v2026.11.09 the supplemental table obs_ctd_full is published with most casts missing for 22 cruises between April 2015 and April 2026: a fault in the release export, found by the release’s maintainers while this page was being written and now being corrected, not a fault in the data. Its trace is in the catalog, which lists 24 of that table’s objects more than once. Every departure, ranking and layer mean on this page is computed from the thinned series (obs_env) and the climatology table, which are complete. The one-metre table is read for seven cruises only, fall 2026 and the six November cruises of the baseline (2001, 2002, 2005, 2009, 2010, 2013), and for each of them the published object holds every cast the release’s sample table lists (924 casts in all, checked each time the page is rendered).
  • Cause. These measurements describe the water. They do not attribute it, and neither, yet, does NOAA: a marine heatwave has been in place off California since 2025 and a strong El Niño arrived on top of it.

9 Methods

  • Data. CalCOFI Integrated Database release v2026.11.09, read through its catalog with calcofi4r (cc_catalog(), cc_release_sources()); every object is listed with its URL under Data sources. Tables: obs_env (the thinned CTD series and the bottle series, with the release’s quality predicate qual_ok), climatology, obs_ctd_full (one-metre CTD casts of the cruise), sample, sample_measurement, cruise.
  • A cell is one cruise × station × 10 m depth bin of one series: the mean of its quality-ok values.
  • A departure is a cell minus the climatology row of the same series, station, depth bin and measurement type for the cruise’s month (cruise.month_median, the month of its median cast). The seasonal departure uses the row’s season_mean (December–February, March–May, June–August, September–November).
  • A layer mean averages a station’s profile over every 10 m bin of the layer, after linear interpolation in depth between sampled bins (never across more than 60 m, never beyond the sampled range), and requires every bin. A cruise mean averages the stations.
  • The map’s shading is ordinary kriging by calcofi4r::cc_interpolate(), the interpolator of the Explorer’s contour maps, clipped to the hull of the stations (plus 15 km), masked over land and limited to the range of the measured values. Colours are the cmocean maps (Thyng et al. 2016). Density is TEOS-10 potential density anomaly, from the gsw package.
  • Mixed-layer depth is the release’s mld_sigma_theta_0125, in the registry’s words “Mixed-layer depth, sigma-theta increase of 0.125 kg/m3 from 10 m (Levitus 1982)” (calcofi4db::ctd_mld(criterion = ‘sigma_theta’, threshold = 0.125, ref_depth = 10) on the 1 m bins; an alternative criterion published beside the headline mld_sigma_theta_002 (questions Q01)), with its own November normal. The release’s headline criterion is stricter and stops at a thin warm skin on some casts; the looser one is used here because the question is how deep the warm layer reaches.
  • The whole-record yardstick compares a cell with the mean of the other cruises, before fall 2026, of the same series at the same station, calendar month and depth bin, where at least five exist. Two casts that hold bad values (shown above) are left out of it and of the per-event maxima.
  • Salinity across events uses the bottle series’ values and normals (bottle casts end in 2021), and the fall 2026 CTD against the same bottle normals, because the CTD salinity normal carries unflagged spikes.
  • Published values quoted under context were each read in the source cited, or in its abstract where the table says so; every quotation was checked against a saved copy of the text. Each entry of the bibliography was built from its Crossref or DataCite record.
  • Outside sources (buoys, the Scripps Pier shore station, satellite analyses, Argo, the glider index) are fetched by scripts/temperature_anomaly_outside_sources.py and kept as small tables in data/2026-11_temperature-anomaly/, because the buoy files hold only the last 45 days.

12 Code

Every figure and table above has its code folded beside it. The steps that run before the summary are hidden at the top of the page so that the summary comes first; they are shown here, in the order they run. The whole notebook is 2026-11_temperature-anomaly.qmd.

Setup

code 
librarian::shelf(
  calcofi4r, cmocean, DBI, dplyr, DT, duckdb, ggplot2, ggrepel, glue, gsw, here, htmltools, knitr,
  patchwork, purrr, readr, rnaturalearth, sf, stringr, terra, tibble, tidyr,
  quiet = T)
options(readr.show_col_types = F, knitr.kable.NA = "")

# constants ----
VER       <- "v2026.11.09"    # the release this page is pinned to (latest.txt on 2026-11-13)
CRUISE    <- "2026-11-33P4"   # R/V Sally Ride, 31 October to 7 November 2026
core      <- c("093.3 028.0", "093.3 030.0")   # the two stations at the heart of the warm layer
BASE_URL  <- "https://storage.googleapis.com/calcofi-db"
DIR_DATA  <- here("data/2026-11_temperature-anomaly")   # small tables this page writes or keeps
DIR_CACHE <- Sys.getenv("CALCOFI_CACHE_DIR", tools::R_user_dir("calcofi", "cache"))
KM_PER_STATION <- 7.386       # +proj=calcofi: a line is equidistant, 7.386 km (4 nmi) per station unit
ANOM_MAX  <- 13               # the top of the departure scale, shared by the map and the section (°C)
dir.create(DIR_DATA, showWarnings = F, recursive = T)

# brand v2 inks (https://calcofi.io/brand/v2/theme.css) ----
INK      <- "#182b49"
MUTED    <- "#66686a"
GRID     <- "#e4e4e4"
SAND     <- "#f5f0e6"
STONE    <- "#b6b1a9"
COL_2026 <- "#b3261e"
COL_2015 <- "#c69214"
COL_NORM <- "#00629b"

# number formats: one decimal, a signed departure with a true minus, thousands ----
f1  <- function(x, d = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
fs  <- function(x, d = 1) sub("-", "−", sprintf(paste0("%+.", d, "f"), x), fixed = T)
fk  <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = T)
fsa <- function(x, d = 0) ifelse(!is.na(x) & abs(x) < 0.5 * 10^-d, formatC(0, format = "f", digits = d), fs(x, d))   # axis labels: a bare 0
nb  <- function(x) gsub("–", "\u2060–\u2060", gsub("-", "\u2011", x, fixed = T), fixed = T)   # no line break inside a key or a range
dt_ <- function(d, ...) datatable(
  d, rownames = F, class = "compact stripe", extensions = "Buttons",
  options = list(dom = "Bfrtip", pageLength = 12, buttons = c("copy", "csv")), ...)

# plot theme ----
theme_story <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text                  = element_text(colour = INK),
      axis.text             = element_text(colour = MUTED),
      panel.grid.major      = element_line(colour = GRID, linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.grid.minor      = element_blank(),
      plot.title            = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(1.12)),
      plot.subtitle         = element_text(colour = MUTED, size = rel(0.9), margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.caption          = element_text(colour = MUTED, size = rel(0.72), hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.15),
      plot.title.position   = "plot",
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      strip.text            = element_text(face = "bold", colour = INK, hjust = 0),
      legend.position       = "none")}

Release objects, through the catalog

code 
# the release catalog is the only source of object URLs (calcofi4r::cc_catalog() / cc_release_sources()):
# every table below is read from the URLs the catalog lists, never from a path built by hand
CAT   <- cc_catalog(VER)
con   <- dbConnect(duckdb())
d_src <- tibble()   # every object this page reads: the table under "Data sources"

# a release object by its catalog URL, kept in a local cache (objects are content-addressed and immutable) ----
mirror <- function(url) {
  path <- file.path(DIR_CACHE, sub(paste0(BASE_URL, "/"), "", url, fixed = T))
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    dir.create(dirname(path), recursive = T, showWarnings = F)
    curl::curl_download(url, paste0(path, ".part"), quiet = T)
    file.rename(paste0(path, ".part"), path)}
  path}

# a DuckDB view over one release table: all of its objects, or the partitions named in `parts` ----
release_view <- function(table, parts = NULL, cols = "*", name = table) {
  src  <- cc_release_sources(CAT, table)
  urls <- src$urls
  if (!is.null(parts))
    urls <- unique(unlist(lapply(parts, \(p) grep(glue("={p}/"), urls, fixed = T, value = T))))   # the catalog lists some objects twice
  stopifnot(length(urls) >= 1, is.null(parts) || length(urls) == length(parts))
  files <- vapply(urls, mirror, "", USE.NAMES = F)
  dbExecute(con, glue(
    "CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW {name} AS SELECT {cols} FROM read_parquet(",
    "[{paste0(\"'\", files, \"'\", collapse = ', ')}], hive_partitioning = {tolower(src$hive)}, union_by_name = true)"))
  d_src <<- bind_rows(d_src, tibble(
    table = table, partition = if (is.null(parts)) NA_character_ else parts, url = urls, mb = file.size(files) / 1e6))
  invisible(urls)}

# the tables this page reads ----
release_view("cruise")
release_view("sample", cols = "* EXCLUDE (geom)")
release_view("sample_measurement")
release_view("measurement_type")
release_view("obs_env",      parts = c("temperature_ave", "temperature", "salinity_ave_corr", "salinity"))
release_view("climatology",  parts = c("temperature_ave", "temperature", "salinity_ave_corr", "salinity", "mld_sigma_theta_0125"))
release_view("obs_ctd_full", parts = CRUISE)

Every temperature cell and its departure

code 
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE cell AS
-- every temperature cell in the record with its departure from the release's own climatology.
-- a CELL is one cruise x station (site_key) x 10 m depth bin of one dataset: the mean of its quality-ok observations.
-- its baseline is the climatology row of the SAME dataset, station, depth bin and measurement type for the CRUISE's
-- month (obs_env.cruise_month = cruise.month_median), the rule every CalCOFI app applies. A cell whose month has no
-- monthly baseline keeps anom NULL: never 0. The seasonal baseline (the cruise's season) rides along as anom_season.
WITH o AS (
  SELECT dataset_key, measurement_type, cruise_key, site_key, depth_bin,
         any_value(cruise_month) AS cruise_month, any_value(year) AS cruise_year,
         avg(value) AS v, count(*) AS n_obs, avg(depth_min_m) AS depth_m,
         avg(latitude) AS latitude, avg(longitude) AS longitude, min(datetime) AS datetime
  FROM obs_env
  WHERE measurement_type IN ('temperature_ave', 'temperature')          -- CTD sensor-pair average; bottle (QC'd)
    AND dataset_key IN ('calcofi_ctd-cast', 'calcofi_bottle')
    AND qual_ok AND value IS NOT NULL AND depth_bin IS NOT NULL AND site_key IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ALL)
SELECT o.*,
       TRY_CAST(split_part(o.site_key, ' ', 1) AS DOUBLE) AS line,
       TRY_CAST(split_part(o.site_key, ' ', 2) AS DOUBLE) AS station,
       c.clim_mean, c.clim_sd, c.clim_n, c.n_cruises, c.season_mean, c.season_sd, c.season_n_cruises,
       o.v - c.clim_mean   AS anom,
       o.v - c.season_mean AS anom_season
FROM o
LEFT JOIN climatology c
  ON c.dataset_key = o.dataset_key AND c.measurement_type = o.measurement_type AND c.site_key = o.site_key
 AND c.month = o.cruise_month AND c.depth_bin = o.depth_bin

Cruises, and the one-metre casts of the cruise

code 
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE cruise_ref AS
-- one row per cruise: its dates, its month (the median cast month) and the stage of its CTD casts
SELECT c.cruise_key, c.year, c.month_median AS cruise_month, c.date_min, c.date_max, c.date_median, c.ship_name,
       (SELECT string_agg(DISTINCT s.data_stage, ', ' ORDER BY s.data_stage) FROM sample s
        WHERE s.cruise_key = c.cruise_key AND s.dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND s.sample_type = 'cast') AS ctd_stage
FROM cruise c
code 
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE cast_1m AS
-- the November 2026 casts at the CTD's full 1 m resolution (obs_ctd_full), with their station
SELECT s.site_key, f.sample_key, right(f.sample_key, 1) AS direction, f.depth_min_m AS depth_m,
       f.measurement_type, f.measurement_value AS value, f.measurement_qual, f.datetime, f.latitude, f.longitude
FROM obs_ctd_full f JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
WHERE f.measurement_type IN ('temperature_ave', 'temperature_1', 'temperature_2', 'salinity_1', 'salinity_2',
                             'salinity_ave_corr', 'sigma_theta_1', 'salinity_btl', 'oxygen_btl_ml_l', 'oxygen_ml_l_1')

Profiles on every 10 m bin, and layer means

code 
CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO interp_profile(col) AS TABLE
-- an anomaly (or temperature) profile on every 10 m bin from 0 to 190 m: linear interpolation IN DEPTH between the
-- bins that were sampled (never across more than 60 m, never beyond the deepest or above the shallowest sampled bin,
-- never in time or between stations). It puts the bottle series (standard depths) on the CTD's footing.
WITH a AS (SELECT dataset_key, cruise_key, site_key, depth_bin, col AS a FROM cell WHERE col IS NOT NULL AND depth_bin < 260),
casts AS (SELECT DISTINCT dataset_key, cruise_key, site_key FROM a),
t AS (SELECT c.*, b.depth_bin FROM casts c, (SELECT unnest(range(0, 200, 10)) AS depth_bin) b)
SELECT t.dataset_key, t.cruise_key, t.site_key, t.depth_bin,
       CASE WHEN lo.depth_bin = hi.depth_bin THEN lo.a
            WHEN hi.depth_bin - lo.depth_bin <= 60 THEN lo.a + (hi.a - lo.a) * (t.depth_bin - lo.depth_bin) / (hi.depth_bin - lo.depth_bin) END AS a
FROM t
ASOF LEFT JOIN a lo ON lo.dataset_key = t.dataset_key AND lo.cruise_key = t.cruise_key AND lo.site_key = t.site_key AND lo.depth_bin <= t.depth_bin
ASOF LEFT JOIN a hi ON hi.dataset_key = t.dataset_key AND hi.cruise_key = t.cruise_key AND hi.site_key = t.site_key AND hi.depth_bin >= t.depth_bin
code 
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE prof AS
-- the three interpolated profiles side by side. The key columns are the USING columns (coalesced over the three sides):
-- a cruise in a month with no monthly normal (September 1997) has no row on the anom side and must keep its keys.
SELECT dataset_key, cruise_key, site_key, depth_bin, m.a AS anom, s.a AS anom_season, v.a AS temp
FROM interp_profile(anom) m
FULL JOIN interp_profile(anom_season) s USING (dataset_key, cruise_key, site_key, depth_bin)
FULL JOIN interp_profile(v) v USING (dataset_key, cruise_key, site_key, depth_bin)
code 
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE station_layer AS
-- one row per cast x layer: the depth-mean where the layer is complete (every 10 m bin of it present)
WITH l AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('surface (0-10 m)', 0, 0), ('0-50 m', 0, 40), ('50-200 m', 50, 190), ('0-200 m', 0, 190)) AS t(layer, b0, b1))
SELECT p.dataset_key, p.cruise_key, p.site_key, l.layer,
       TRY_CAST(split_part(p.site_key, ' ', 1) AS DOUBLE) AS line, TRY_CAST(split_part(p.site_key, ' ', 2) AS DOUBLE) AS station,
       CASE WHEN count(p.anom)        = (l.b1 - l.b0) / 10 + 1 THEN avg(p.anom) END        AS anom,
       CASE WHEN count(p.anom_season) = (l.b1 - l.b0) / 10 + 1 THEN avg(p.anom_season) END AS anom_season,
       CASE WHEN count(p.temp)        = (l.b1 - l.b0) / 10 + 1 THEN avg(p.temp) END        AS temp
FROM prof p JOIN l ON p.depth_bin BETWEEN l.b0 AND l.b1
GROUP BY p.dataset_key, p.cruise_key, p.site_key, l.layer, l.b0, l.b1

Each cruise over the fall 2026 stations, and on shared stations

code 
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE cruise_layer AS
-- every cruise's layer mean over ONE fixed set of stations: the ones the November 2026 cruise occupied.
-- `covered`: the cruise occupied at least 60 % of the stations November 2026 has for that layer.
WITH fp AS (SELECT DISTINCT site_key FROM cell WHERE cruise_key = '2026-11-33P4' AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast'),
n26 AS (SELECT layer, count(anom) AS n_ref, count(anom_season) AS n_ref_season FROM station_layer WHERE cruise_key = '2026-11-33P4' GROUP BY layer),
x AS (
  SELECT s.dataset_key, s.cruise_key, s.layer,
         count(s.anom) AS n_sta, avg(s.anom) AS anom, max(s.anom) AS anom_max_station,
         count(s.anom_season) AS n_sta_season, avg(s.anom_season) AS anom_season, avg(s.temp) AS temp
  FROM station_layer s SEMI JOIN fp USING (site_key)
  GROUP BY ALL)
SELECT x.*, n26.n_ref, n26.n_ref_season,
       x.n_sta >= 0.6 * n26.n_ref AS covered, x.n_sta_season >= 0.6 * n26.n_ref_season AS covered_season,
       c.year, c.cruise_month, c.date_min, c.date_max
FROM x JOIN n26 USING (layer) LEFT JOIN cruise_ref c USING (cruise_key)
code 
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE paired AS
-- the strictest comparison: November 2026 against every other cruise ON THE STATIONS THEY SHARE, by three yardsticks:
-- the departure from the monthly normal, from the seasonal normal, and the layer's temperature itself (no baseline)
WITH ref AS (SELECT site_key, layer, anom AS a26, anom_season AS s26, temp AS t26 FROM station_layer WHERE cruise_key = '2026-11-33P4' AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast')
SELECT s.dataset_key, s.cruise_key, s.layer,
       count(*)           FILTER (WHERE s.anom IS NOT NULL AND r.a26 IS NOT NULL)        AS n_month,
       avg(s.anom)        FILTER (WHERE s.anom IS NOT NULL AND r.a26 IS NOT NULL)        AS anom_other,
       avg(r.a26)         FILTER (WHERE s.anom IS NOT NULL AND r.a26 IS NOT NULL)        AS anom_2026,
       count(*)           FILTER (WHERE s.anom_season IS NOT NULL AND r.s26 IS NOT NULL) AS n_season,
       avg(s.anom_season) FILTER (WHERE s.anom_season IS NOT NULL AND r.s26 IS NOT NULL) AS season_other,
       avg(r.s26)         FILTER (WHERE s.anom_season IS NOT NULL AND r.s26 IS NOT NULL) AS season_2026,
       count(*)           FILTER (WHERE s.temp IS NOT NULL AND r.t26 IS NOT NULL)        AS n_temp,
       avg(s.temp)        FILTER (WHERE s.temp IS NOT NULL AND r.t26 IS NOT NULL)        AS temp_other,
       avg(r.t26)         FILTER (WHERE s.temp IS NOT NULL AND r.t26 IS NOT NULL)        AS temp_2026
FROM station_layer s JOIN ref r USING (site_key, layer)
WHERE s.cruise_key <> '2026-11-33P4'
GROUP BY ALL

The numbers of the summary

code 
q <- function(sql, ...) dbGetQuery(con, glue_sql(sql, ..., .con = con)) |> as_tibble()

# two casts hold bad values, not warm water (shown under "Single measurements"): left out where events are compared ----
invisible(dbExecute(con, "
  CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW cell_ok AS
  SELECT * FROM cell
  WHERE NOT (cruise_key = '1994-01-31JD' AND dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND site_key = '093.3 028.0' AND depth_bin >= 510)
    AND NOT (cruise_key = '1959-10-31OR' AND site_key = '093.3 035.0')"))

# the record cell and the previous record ----
d_cell26 <- q("SELECT * FROM cell WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND anom IS NOT NULL ORDER BY anom DESC")
top      <- d_cell26[1, ]
prev     <- q("SELECT * FROM cell WHERE cruise_key <> {CRUISE} AND anom IS NOT NULL ORDER BY anom DESC LIMIT 1")
d_share  <- q("
  WITH r AS (SELECT cruise_key, anom, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY anom DESC) AS rk FROM cell WHERE anom IS NOT NULL)
  SELECT count(*) AS n_cells, count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS n_cruises,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE rk <= 50  AND cruise_key = {CRUISE}) AS of_top_50,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE rk <= 100 AND cruise_key = {CRUISE}) AS of_top_100,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND anom > {prev$anom}) AS n_above_prev,
         min(substr(cruise_key, 1, 4)) AS yr0
  FROM r")
n_cruises_all <- q("SELECT count(DISTINCT cruise_key) AS n FROM cell")$n

# each earlier warm event's largest single departure, by the monthly normal and by the seasonal one ----
d_evmax <- q("
  WITH ev AS (SELECT * FROM (VALUES ('1957–59', 1957, 1959), ('1982–83', 1982, 1983), ('1997–98', 1997, 1998), ('2014–16', 2014, 2016)) t(event, y0, y1))
  SELECT ev.event, max(c.anom) AS anom, arg_max(c.cruise_key, c.anom) AS cruise_key, arg_max(c.site_key, c.anom) AS site_key,
         arg_max(c.depth_bin, c.anom) AS depth_bin, max(c.anom_season) AS anom_s, arg_max(c.cruise_key, c.anom_season) AS cruise_s,
         arg_max(c.site_key, c.anom_season) AS site_s, arg_max(c.depth_bin, c.anom_season) AS bin_s
  FROM cell_ok c JOIN ev ON c.cruise_year BETWEEN ev.y0 AND ev.y1 GROUP BY ev.event ORDER BY ev.event")
evm <- function(e) d_evmax[d_evmax$event == e, ]
sta <- function(site_key) sub("^0", "", gsub(" 0+", " ", site_key))      # "093.3 030.0" -> "93.3 30.0"
stopifnot(abs(c(evm("1982–83")$anom, evm("1997–98")$anom, evm("1997–98")$anom_s) - 6) < 0.6)   # "near +6 °C" in the summary

# layer means over the stations the cruise occupied ----
d_layer <- q("SELECT * FROM cruise_layer WHERE covered") |>
  mutate(series = if_else(dataset_key == "calcofi_bottle", "bottle", "CTD"))
lay <- function(layer_, cruise_ = CRUISE, ds = "calcofi_ctd-cast") d_layer |>
  filter(layer == layer_, cruise_key == cruise_, dataset_key == ds)
runner <- function(layer_) d_layer |> filter(layer == layer_, cruise_key != CRUISE) |> slice_max(anom, n = 1, with_ties = F)

# the cruise, station by station ----
d_sta <- q("
  SELECT s.site_key, s.line, s.station, s.layer, s.anom, s.anom_season, s.temp, p.lat, p.lon, p.t0
  FROM station_layer s
  JOIN (SELECT site_key, avg(latitude) AS lat, avg(longitude) AS lon, min(datetime) AS t0 FROM cell
        WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND depth_bin = 0 GROUP BY site_key) p USING (site_key)
  WHERE s.cruise_key = {CRUISE}") |>
  mutate(km_offshore = (station - 26.4) * KM_PER_STATION)
sfc   <- d_sta |> filter(layer == "surface (0-10 m)", !is.na(anom))
# the inner Southern California Bight: the stations inshore of the front the cruise crossed
inner <- sfc |> filter((line >= 88 & station <= 37) | (line < 88 & station <= 51))
outer <- sfc |> anti_join(inner, by = "site_key")
stopifnot(min(inner$anom) > max(outer$anom))   # the two groups do not overlap: a front, not a gradient

# salinity and mixed-layer depth on the inshore end of line 93.3 ----
d_sal <- q("
  SELECT o.site_key, o.depth_bin, avg(o.value) AS sal, any_value(c.clim_mean) AS clim, any_value(c.clim_sd) AS sd
  FROM obs_env o LEFT JOIN climatology c
    ON c.measurement_type = o.measurement_type AND c.dataset_key = o.dataset_key AND c.site_key = o.site_key
   AND c.depth_bin = o.depth_bin AND c.month = o.cruise_month
  WHERE o.cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND o.measurement_type = 'salinity_ave_corr' AND o.qual_ok
    AND o.site_key IN ({core*}) AND o.depth_bin <= 40
  GROUP BY ALL")
d_mld <- q("
  SELECT s.site_key, m.measurement_value AS mld, c.clim_mean AS clim, c.n_cruises
  FROM sample_measurement m JOIN sample s USING (sample_key)
  LEFT JOIN climatology c ON c.measurement_type = m.measurement_type AND c.site_key = s.site_key AND c.month = 11 AND c.depth_bin IS NULL
  WHERE s.cruise_key = {CRUISE} AND m.measurement_type = 'mld_sigma_theta_0125'
    AND s.site_key IN ('093.3 026.7', '093.3 028.0', '093.3 030.0')")

mt   <- q("SELECT description, derivation FROM measurement_type WHERE measurement_type = 'mld_sigma_theta_0125'")
cr   <- q("SELECT * FROM cruise_ref WHERE cruise_key = {CRUISE}")
n_st <- n_distinct(d_sta$site_key)
k <- list(
  top_anom   = top$anom,  top_v = top$v, top_clim = top$clim_mean, top_n = top$n_cruises,
  top_site   = top$site_key, top_bin = top$depth_bin, top_date = as.Date(top$datetime),
  top_km     = round((top$station - 26.4) * KM_PER_STATION),
  prev_anom  = prev$anom, prev_cruise = prev$cruise_key,
  l50        = lay("0-50 m")$anom,   l50_n  = lay("0-50 m")$n_sta,   l50_prev  = runner("0-50 m"),
  l200       = lay("50-200 m")$anom, l200_n = lay("50-200 m")$n_sta, l200_prev = runner("50-200 m"),
  feb98      = lay("0-50 m", "1998-02-31JD")$anom,

Temperature and salinity of every cruise in the inner Bight

code 
# temperature and salinity departures of every cruise over the inner-Bight stations, upper 50 m, against the BOTTLE
# series' normals (quality-controlled; the CTD salinity normal carries unflagged spikes). Bottle casts through 2021;
# the fall 2026 cruise from its CTD, whose salinity matches the bottles drawn on board (see "Bottles").
# A station counts when at least three of its five 10 m bins have a value and a normal; a cruise when 8 stations do.
d_tsx <- q("
  WITH o AS (
    SELECT cruise_key, CASE WHEN measurement_type LIKE 'salinity%' THEN 'S' ELSE 'T' END AS var, site_key, depth_bin,
           any_value(cruise_month) AS m, avg(value) AS v
    FROM obs_env
    WHERE qual_ok AND depth_bin <= 40 AND site_key IN ({inner$site_key*})
      AND ((dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle'   AND measurement_type IN ('temperature', 'salinity'))
        OR (dataset_key = 'calcofi_ctd-cast' AND measurement_type IN ('temperature_ave', 'salinity_ave_corr') AND cruise_key = {CRUISE}))
    GROUP BY ALL),
  a AS (
    SELECT o.cruise_key, o.var, o.site_key, avg(o.v - c.clim_mean) AS anom
    FROM o JOIN climatology c
      ON c.dataset_key = 'calcofi_bottle' AND c.measurement_type = CASE o.var WHEN 'S' THEN 'salinity' ELSE 'temperature' END
     AND c.site_key = o.site_key AND c.depth_bin = o.depth_bin AND c.month = o.m AND c.clim_mean IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(*) >= 3)
  SELECT a.cruise_key, r.year, r.cruise_month,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE var = 'T') AS n_t, avg(anom) FILTER (WHERE var = 'T') AS t_anom,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE var = 'S') AS n_s, avg(anom) FILTER (WHERE var = 'S') AS s_anom,
         min(anom) FILTER (WHERE var = 'S') AS s_min, max(anom) FILTER (WHERE var = 'S') AS s_max
  FROM a JOIN cruise_ref r USING (cruise_key) GROUP BY ALL
  HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE var = 'T') >= 8 AND count(*) FILTER (WHERE var = 'S') >= 8")
tsx     <- function(cruise) d_tsx |> filter(cruise_key == cruise)
fs0     <- function(x, d = 2) if (abs(x) < 0.5 * 10^-d) f1(0, d) else fs(x, d)   # a departure that rounds to zero carries no sign
ts26    <- tsx(CRUISE)
ts_prev <- d_tsx |> filter(cruise_key != CRUISE) |> slice_max(s_anom, n = 1)
stopifnot(nrow(ts26) == 1, ts26$s_anom > ts_prev$s_anom, ts_prev$cruise_key == "1998-02-31JD", abs(tsx("2015-11-32OC")$s_anom) < 0.05)

Outside sources (scripts/temperature_anomaly_outside_sources.py, run once)

code 
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Outside sources for 2026-11_temperature-anomaly.qmd: measurements that never passed through the CalCOFI pipeline,
for the days and places of the November 2026 CTD casts.

  1. Buoys: NDBC / CDIP buoys and the NOS La Jolla tide station. NDBC's realtime2 files hold the last 45 days only,
     which is why this runs once and its small tables are kept in the repo.
       buoy_stations.csv   every station used: id, name, position, the URL read
       buoys_at_casts.csv  the water temperature reported nearest in time to each cast, for stations within MAX_KM
       buoy_series.csv     hourly mean water temperature of those stations over the whole file (about 45 days)
  2. Satellite analyses at each cast's position on the cast's day, from NOAA CoastWatch West Coast ERDDAP:
     NOAA OISST v2.1 near real time (0.25 degree; `sst` and its `anom` against 1971-2000) and
     JPL MUR v4.1 (0.01 degree; `analysed_sst`, and `sstAnom` against the 2003-2014 MUR climatology).
       satellite_at_casts.csv
  3. Argo float profiles in and around the cruise's box and dates, from the Ifremer ERDDAP.
       argo_profiles.csv
  4. The SCCOOS automated shore station on Scripps Pier (temperature and salinity at the coast, 2013 to now), as daily
     means of the values that pass the station's own quality tests, from the IOOS sensors ERDDAP (Axiom).
       pier_daily.csv
  5. The Southern California Temperature Index of the Scripps glider group (California Underwater Glider Network):
     the temperature departure at 50 m on CalCOFI line 90, coast to 200 km offshore, three-month running mean,
     monthly since 2007, from the group's ERDDAP.
       glider_index.csv
  6. sources.csv: every URL requested, and when.

usage: temperature_anomaly_outside_sources.py <casts.csv> <cache_dir> <out_dir>
  casts.csv is written by the notebook from the release (site_key, cast_id, time_utc, lat, lon, ctd_t_top3m).
  Responses are cached in cache_dir, so a second run repeats no request that already succeeded; ERDDAP answers 503
  under load, and a value it could not serve is left empty and filled by the next run. OUTSIDE_OFFLINE=1 rebuilds the
  tables from the cache alone.
Only cast positions and times go out, to public data services; nothing identifies who asks.
"""
import csv, hashlib, math, os, sys, time, urllib.request
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import datetime, timezone, timedelta

UA      = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (data-check script)"}
MAX_KM  = 15.0     # a buoy is compared with a cast when it is this close
MAX_MIN = 45       # and reported within this many minutes of it
BUOYS   = ["46225", "46254", "46258", "46232", "46086", "46224", "46222", "46025", "46047", "46219", "46069", "46053",
           "46221", "46251", "46253", "46256", "LJAC1"]
SERIES  = ["46225", "46254", "LJAC1", "46258", "46232", "46086", "46221", "46219", "46047"]   # kept as hourly series
NDBC    = "https://www.ndbc.noaa.gov"
ERDDAP  = "https://coastwatch.pfeg.noaa.gov/erddap/griddap/"
ARGO    = "https://erddap.ifremer.fr/erddap/tabledap/ArgoFloats.csv"
PIER    = "https://erddap.sensors.axds.co/erddap/tabledap/scripps-pier-automated-shore-sta-1.csv"
GLIDER  = "https://spraydata.ucsd.edu/erddap/tabledap/socal_index_monthly_v1.csv?time,scti"
SOURCES = []

def fetch(url, cache_dir, name=None, tries=3, wait=4):
  """the body of a URL, from the cache when a previous run already has it; None when the server will not serve it"""
  f = os.path.join(cache_dir, name or hashlib.sha1(url.encode()).hexdigest()[:16] + ".txt")
  if os.path.exists(f) and os.path.getsize(f) > 0:
    SOURCES.append((url, datetime.fromtimestamp(os.path.getmtime(f), timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ"), "ok"))
    return open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
  if os.environ.get("OUTSIDE_OFFLINE"):                        # build the tables from the cache alone, asking no server
    return None
  err = None
  for i in range(tries):
    try:
      with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers=UA), timeout=45) as r:
        body = r.read()
      open(f, "wb").write(body)
      SOURCES.append((url, datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ"), "ok"))
      return body.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    except Exception as e:
      err = e; time.sleep(wait * (i + 1))
  print(f"  not served: {url} ({err})", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
  SOURCES.append((url, datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ"), f"failed: {err}"))
  return None

def km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):
  p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)
  a = math.sin((p2 - p1) / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(math.radians(lon2 - lon1) / 2) ** 2
  return 6371.0 * 2 * math.asin(math.sqrt(a))

def write(path, rows, fields=None):
  with open(path, "w", newline="") as f:
    w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fields or list(rows[0].keys())); w.writeheader(); w.writerows(rows)
  print(f"wrote {path} ({len(rows)} rows)", flush=True)

def glider_index(cache, out):
  txt = fetch(GLIDER, cache, "glider_index_tabledap.csv")
  if txt:
    rows = list(csv.reader(txt.strip().splitlines()))
    write(os.path.join(out, "glider_index.csv"),
          [dict(month=r[0][:7], scti=round(float(r[1]), 3)) for r in rows[2:] if len(r) > 1 and r[1] not in ("", "NaN")])

def main():
  casts_csv, cache, out = sys.argv[1:4]
  os.makedirs(cache, exist_ok=True); os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
  casts = list(csv.DictReader(open(casts_csv)))
  for c in casts:
    c["t"] = datetime.strptime(c["time_utc"], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ").replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
    c["lat"], c["lon"] = float(c["lat"]), float(c["lon"])

  # ---- 1. buoys ----
  tbl = fetch(f"{NDBC}/data/stations/station_table.txt", cache, "station_table.txt")
  pos = {}
  for ln in tbl.splitlines():
    p = ln.split("|")
    if len(p) > 6 and p[0].upper() in BUOYS:
      w = p[6].split()                                         # "32.933 N 117.391 W (...)"
      pos[p[0].upper()] = dict(name=p[4].split(" - ")[0].strip(), lat=float(w[0]) * (1 if w[1] == "N" else -1),
                               lon=float(w[2]) * (-1 if w[3] == "W" else 1))
  stations, pairs, series = [], [], []
  for b in BUOYS:
    url = f"{NDBC}/data/realtime2/{b}.txt"
    txt = fetch(url, cache, f"ndbc_{b}.txt")
    if not txt or b not in pos: continue
    obs = []
    for ln in txt.splitlines():
      p = ln.split()
      if ln.startswith("#") or len(p) < 15 or p[14] == "MM": continue          # column 15 is WTMP, degC
      obs.append((datetime(*map(int, p[:5]), tzinfo=timezone.utc), float(p[14])))
    if not obs: continue
    near = min(km(c["lat"], c["lon"], pos[b]["lat"], pos[b]["lon"]) for c in casts)
    stations.append(dict(buoy=b, name=pos[b]["name"], lat=pos[b]["lat"], lon=pos[b]["lon"], km_to_nearest_cast=round(near, 1),
                         first_utc=min(o[0] for o in obs).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ"), last_utc=max(o[0] for o in obs).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ"),
                         n_obs=len(obs), url=url, page=f"{NDBC}/station_page.php?station={b.lower()}"))
    for c in casts:
      d = km(c["lat"], c["lon"], pos[b]["lat"], pos[b]["lon"])
      if d > MAX_KM: continue
      t, v = min(obs, key=lambda o: abs(o[0] - c["t"]))
      if abs(t - c["t"]) > timedelta(minutes=MAX_MIN): continue
      day = [x for tt, x in obs if abs(tt - c["t"]) <= timedelta(hours=12)]
      pairs.append(dict(site_key=c["site_key"], cast_time_utc=c["time_utc"], ctd_t_top3m=c["ctd_t_top3m"], buoy=b, buoy_name=pos[b]["name"],
                        km_apart=round(d, 1), buoy_time_utc=t.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ"), buoy_wtmp=v,
                        buoy_minus_ctd=round(v - float(c["ctd_t_top3m"]), 2), buoy_24h_min=min(day), buoy_24h_max=max(day)))
    if b in SERIES:
      hours = defaultdict(list)
      for t, v in obs: hours[t.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:00Z")].append(v)
      series += [dict(buoy=b, hour_utc=h, wtmp=round(sum(v) / len(v), 2), n=len(v)) for h, v in sorted(hours.items())]
  pairs.sort(key=lambda r: (r["cast_time_utc"], r["km_apart"]))
  write(os.path.join(out, "buoy_stations.csv"), stations)
  write(os.path.join(out, "buoys_at_casts.csv"), pairs)
  write(os.path.join(out, "buoy_series.csv"), series)

  # ---- 3. Argo (before the satellites: it is one quick request) ----
  t0 = (min(c["t"] for c in casts) - timedelta(days=16)).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT00:00:00Z")
  t1 = (max(c["t"] for c in casts) + timedelta(days=6)).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT00:00:00Z")
  box = (min(c["lat"] for c in casts) - 0.7, max(c["lat"] for c in casts) + 0.8, min(c["lon"] for c in casts) - 0.6, max(c["lon"] for c in casts) + 0.4)
  url = (f"{ARGO}?platform_number,cycle_number,time,latitude,longitude,pres,temp,psal,temp_qc&time%3E={t0}&time%3C={t1}"
         f"&latitude%3E={box[0]:.2f}&latitude%3C={box[1]:.2f}&longitude%3E={box[2]:.2f}&longitude%3C={box[3]:.2f}&pres%3C=160")
  txt = fetch(url, cache, "argo.csv")
  if txt:
    rows = list(csv.reader(txt.strip().splitlines()))
    write(os.path.join(out, "argo_profiles.csv"), [dict(zip(rows[0], r)) for r in rows[2:]], rows[0])

  # ---- 4. Scripps Pier: daily means of temperature and of salinity, each where its own QC aggregate is 1 (pass) ----
  day = {}
  for var, key in (("sea_water_temperature_ctd", "temp"), ("sea_water_practical_salinity_ctd", "sal")):
    txt = fetch(f"{PIER}?time,{var}&{var}_qc_agg=1&orderByMean(%22time/1day%22)", cache, f"pier_{key}_daily.csv")
    for ln in (txt or "").strip().splitlines()[2:]:
      t, v = ln.split(",")[:2]
      if v not in ("NaN", ""): day.setdefault(t[:10], {})[key] = round(float(v), 3)
  if day:
    write(os.path.join(out, "pier_daily.csv"), [dict(date=d, temp=v.get("temp", ""), sal=v.get("sal", "")) for d, v in sorted(day.items())])

  # ---- 5. the glider group's temperature index: one small file, month (the centre of the three-month mean) and value ----
  glider_index(cache, out)

  # ---- 2. satellite analyses ----
  # OISST: one gridded request per day over the cruise's box. MUR: one point request per cast and variable.
  lat0, lat1 = min(c["lat"] for c in casts) - 0.3, max(c["lat"] for c in casts) + 0.3
  lon0, lon1 = min(c["lon"] for c in casts) - 0.3, max(c["lon"] for c in casts) + 0.3
  def oisst(var, day):
    q = f"{var}%5B({day}T12:00:00Z)%5D%5B(0.0)%5D%5B({lat0:.2f}):1:({lat1:.2f})%5D%5B({lon0:.2f}):1:({lon1:.2f})%5D"
    txt = fetch(f"{ERDDAP}ncdcOisst21NrtAgg_LonPM180.csv?{q}", cache, f"oisst_{var}_{day}.csv")
    pts = []
    for ln in (txt or "").strip().splitlines()[2:]:
      p = ln.split(",")
      if p[-1] not in ("NaN", ""): pts.append((float(p[-3]), float(p[-2]), float(p[-1])))
    return pts
  def nearest(pts, c, max_km=25):
    if not pts: return None
    la, lo, v = min(pts, key=lambda q: km(c["lat"], c["lon"], q[0], q[1]))
    return round(v, 2) if km(c["lat"], c["lon"], la, lo) <= max_km else None
  def mur(ds, var, c):
    day = c["t"].strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    q = f"{var}%5B({day}T09:00:00Z)%5D%5B({c['lat']:.3f})%5D%5B({c['lon']:.3f})%5D"
    txt = fetch(f"{ERDDAP}{ds}.csv?{q}", cache, f"mur_{var}_{day}_{c['site_key'].replace(' ', '_')}.csv", tries=2)
    try: return round(float(txt.strip().splitlines()[2].split(",")[-1]), 2)
    except Exception: return None
  grids = {day: (oisst("sst", day), oisst("anom", day)) for day in sorted({c["t"].strftime("%Y-%m-%d") for c in casts})}
  sat = []
  for c in casts:
    g = grids[c["t"].strftime("%Y-%m-%d")]
    sat.append(dict(site_key=c["site_key"], cast_time_utc=c["time_utc"], lat=c["lat"], lon=c["lon"], ctd_t_top3m=c["ctd_t_top3m"],
                    oisst_sst=nearest(g[0], c), oisst_anom=nearest(g[1], c),
                    mur_sst=mur("jplMURSST41", "analysed_sst", c), mur_anom=mur("jplMURSST41anom1day", "sstAnom", c)))
    print("  ", sat[-1]["site_key"], sat[-1]["ctd_t_top3m"], sat[-1]["oisst_sst"], sat[-1]["oisst_anom"], sat[-1]["mur_sst"], sat[-1]["mur_anom"], flush=True)
  write(os.path.join(out, "satellite_at_casts.csv"), sat)
  for k in ("oisst_sst", "oisst_anom", "mur_sst", "mur_anom"):
    print(f"  {k}: {sum(r[k] is not None for r in sat)} of {len(sat)} casts", flush=True)

  write(os.path.join(out, "sources.csv"), [dict(url=u, accessed_utc=t, status=s) for u, t, s in SOURCES])

if __name__ == "__main__":
  main()

The animation is a page of its own in the Explorer’s repository, driven by one clock and stepped frame by frame into the video: story/elnino-2026/ at the commit it was rendered from (CalCOFI/explore#55). render.sh is the whole pipeline in one command: it derives the page’s data from the analysis database (build_data.sql), builds the page, captures 900 frames in headless Chrome (capture.mjs) and encodes them with ffmpeg. Its files, read from that commit:

story/elnino-2026/README.md (136 lines) 
# The 2026 warm water off Southern California, in 30 seconds

A story page of its own in this repo: one fixed 1920 × 1080 stage driven by **one clock** (`t`, 0 to 30 s), so the
same page plays live in a browser and is stepped frame by frame into a video. It is not part of the Explorer: it has
its own Vite root and its own `tsconfig.json` here, `npm run build` and `npm test` never see it, and nothing in `src/`
changed.

What it draws is the Explorer's own, imported rather than copied:

| piece | from |
|---|---|
| colour ramps (cmocean *thermal* for temperature, *balance* for the difference from normal) | `src/ramps.ts` |
| the interpolated maps and their isolines (thin-plate spline, blank beyond 60 km of a station, land clipped) | `src/contour.ts` + `src/contour.worker.ts` |
| the sea floor (GEBCO 2025 terrain PMTiles, decoded in the page) and its depth ramp | `src/basemap.ts` (`BATHY_URL`, `BATHY_RAMP`); the decode is `src/curtain.tsx`'s `loadMosaic()`, repeated in `page/terrain.ts` because that module is React |
| the 3-D section (a curtain along the line, the floor as a mesh, vertical exaggeration baked in) | the recipe of `src/curtain.tsx`, as a smaller deck.gl scene in `page/main.ts` |
| fonts and tokens | the brand's own files, copied verbatim into `page/brand/` (calcofi.io/brand/v2: `fonts.css`, `theme.css`, Source Sans 3, Teko), dark |

## Two scales, fixed for the whole film

| | ramp | range | legend ticks |
|---|---|---|---|
| temperature at the surface | cmocean *thermal* | 11 to 26 °C | 12, 16, 20, 24 |
| difference from normal (maps, year bars and the section) | cmocean *balance* | −13 to +13 °C | −12, −6, 0, +6, +12 |

Neither is ever rescaled: a redder frame is a warmer ocean. The consequence is intended and is the story: ordinary
years are pale, 2014–15 pink, 2026 red, and the darkest red appears only under the surface in the last beat.

## The beats

| t (s) | beat | words on screen |
|---|---|---|
| 0 – 5.2 | The nine November cruises of the 1993–2013 baseline, one after another: the ship's track, each station at the surface (0–10 m) coloured by its temperature. The first is on screen from the first frame and holds 1.2 s; the others 0.5 s each. | "November" · the year · "Every fall, a ship measures the ocean off California" · the ship and its station count (stations with a 0–10 m CTD value on that cruise: the dots on screen) |
| 5.2 – 8.2 | All of them together: each station's values close into one, the release's own November normal there (a station with fewer than five cruises has none, and its dots leave). | "1993–2013" · "All of them together: the normal" · "Normal = the 1993–2013 average for November (9 cruises)" |
| 8.2 – 11 | The normal interpolated: first on a coarse regular grid, drawn as its cells, then the map with its isotherms. | "The normal, mapped between the stations" · "Normal = the 1993–2013 average for November" |
| 11 – 15 | The next year, 2014: its track, its stations, its grid, its map. | "2014" · "The next year: one cruise, its stations, its map" · "75 stations" |
| 15 – 17 | The same cruise as its difference from the normal. | "The same cruise, as its difference from normal" · "Red is warmer than normal, blue is cooler" |
| 17 – 24 | Each November since, 2015 to 2026, against the same normal; 2026 holds two seconds. | the year · "Each November since, against the same normal" · the station count; on 2026: "At the surface: 5 to 8 °C warmer than normal near the coast" |
| 24 – 30 | The camera tilts. The map splits along line 93.3: the half behind stays as the sea surface, the half in front leaves, and the section hangs below it: the difference from normal, surface to 200 m, all seven stations, vertical exaggeration × 300. | "Line 93.3, off San Diego" · "2026" · "+12.8 °C" · "at 40–50 m depth: the largest departure in CalCOFI's record, 1949–2026" · "25 °C water down to 55 m" |

Throughout: a *preliminary data* pill on any cruise whose CTD casts are not `final` in the release (2021 onward); the
credit "CalCOFI · calcofi.io · CTD casts · release v2026.11.09".

**The strip** along the bottom says which cruise, out of all of them. Every November cruise is a dot on the years'
line (the other months' CTD cruises a faint texture behind it); the one on screen is yellow with its year under it;
2018 and 2020, whose fall cruise ran in October, are two empty dashed slots marked "no November cruise" (found from
the data, not listed). From 2014 on each cruise the film has played keeps a bar: its mean surface difference from normal **over the
stations the 2026 cruise occupied** (`cruises.json` `mean_anom_fp`), so the bars compare the same stations every year.

## Where each number on screen comes from

No number is typed in `page/main.ts`. `build_data.sql` writes them, and stops the build if one cannot be said.

| on screen | field of `page/data/` | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| "+12.8 °C" | `facts.json` `max_anom` | the largest departure of any cell of the cruise (station × 10 m bin) from the release's November normal |
| "at 40–50 m depth" | `facts.json` `max_anom_bin` (and `max_anom_station` for the ring on the section) | that cell's bin and station |
| "CalCOFI's record, 1949–2026" | `facts.json` `record_from`, `record_to` | the first and last cruise year in the CTD and bottle series |
| "25 °C water down to 55 m" | `facts.json` `layer_temp`, `layer_depth` | at the core stations (28 and 30) the mean of the 1 m bins of the upper 50 m, rounded; and the deepest 1 m bin, counted down from the surface without a break, still within 0.5 °C of it |
| "5 to 8 °C warmer than normal near the coast" | `facts.json` `coast_min`, `coast_max`, rounded | the 0–10 m departures at the 17 stations of the inner Southern California Bight ((line ≥ 88 and station ≤ 37) or (line < 88 and station ≤ 51)). The other 18 stations run `offshore_min` to `offshore_max`; the build fails if the two ranges overlap |
| the year bars and "+4.3 °C" over the current one | `cruises.json` `mean_anom_fp` | the mean 0–10 m departure over the 2026 cruise's stations |
| "9 cruises", "75 stations", the ship | `cruises.json` (`n_stations`, `ship`) | counted from the release: the baseline's November cruises; the stations of a cruise that have a 0–10 m CTD value (the dots on screen, which can be fewer than the cruise occupied) |
| the empty slots, "no November cruise" | derived in the page | the years from 2014 with no November cruise in `strip.json` |
| "release v2026.11.09" | `release.json` | the release the analysis database was built from |

That the largest departure of the cruise is also the largest "in CalCOFI's record" is the finding of
`analysis/` (out/findings.md); the page only repeats it.

## Files

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `build_data.sh`, `build_data.sql` | Derive `page/data/*.json` from the analysis database (`analysis/01`–`04`, which read release objects through the catalog). Deterministic: no timestamp, no network. |
| `page/data/*.json` | `cruises` (the 20 November cruises and their roles), `stations` (cruise × station at 0–10 m: position, time, temperature, normal, difference), `normal` (the November climatology at 0–10 m), `strip` (every CTD cruise), `section` (line 93.3, November 2026, every 10 m bin), `facts`, `release`. Committed, so the page builds without the database. |
| `page/index.html`, `page/style.css` | The stage: the canvas, the column of words, the two legends, the strip. |
| `page/main.ts` | The clock, the beats, the deck.gl scene, the words. `layersAt(t)`, `camAt(t)`, `wordsAt(t)`, `stripSvg(t)` are pure functions of `t`. `selfCheck()` verifies that the section stays in the frame through the whole camera move. |
| `page/terrain.ts` | The terrain mosaic, the flat shaded sea floor of the bird's-eye beats, and the 3-D floor mesh: the terrain itself beside the section's line, low-passed away from it (an island at × 300 is a needle otherwise), fading into the ground with distance. |
| `page/brand/` | The brand's fonts and tokens as files (see its README). |
| `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json` | The page's own Vite root (dev 5180, preview 5181, `dist/` here, git-ignored) and type check. |
| `capture.mjs` | Headless Chrome (puppeteer-core): waits for `window.__story.ready`, stops if the page's check fails, steps `setT(k / 30)`, screenshots each frame, encodes with ffmpeg. `--shots 3.2,12.5` writes single frames instead; `--query cam3=8.84,66,-32,1270,452` tries another 3-D camera. |
| `capture/webgl_probe.mjs` | Proves that headless Chrome draws WebGL2 on this machine (it does: ANGLE on Metal, default flags). |
| `capture/strings.mjs` | Lists every string the page's DOM puts on screen, beat by beat, with the second it first appears: the audit to check against the findings. |
| `render.sh` | All of it in one command. |
| `analysis/` | The findings (Job 1): owned by that work, not by the page. |

## Re-render

Needs: the analysis database (`analysis/`, see `analysis/findings.template.md`), `npm ci`, Google Chrome, `ffmpeg`
(`brew install ffmpeg`).

```sh
# from the repo root, on branch story-elnino-2026
story/elnino-2026/render.sh                              # the deliverables, about 2.5 minutes
story/elnino-2026/render.sh try_v3 --from 24 --to 30     # a rough cut of part of it → $JOB/out/rough/try_v3.mp4
```

`render.sh` with no argument rebuilds `page/data/*.json`, type-checks and builds the page, serves the build on port
5182, captures 900 frames and writes, under `JOB` (default `~/_big/calcofi/story_elnino_2026-11`):

- `out/calcofi_elnino_2026_30s.mp4`: 1920 × 1080, 30 fps, H.264 `yuv420p`, `+faststart`, no audio, 30.0 s;
- `out/calcofi_elnino_2026_poster.png`: the last captured frame, lossless;
- `out/frames/`: a frame per beat pulled from the MP4 (two for beats 6 and 7), five of them also at 390 px wide.

The same, step by step:

```sh
JOB=~/_big/calcofi/story_elnino_2026-11
story/elnino-2026/build_data.sh $JOB                                   # 1. page/data/*.json from $JOB/work/elnino.duckdb
npx tsc -p story/elnino-2026/tsconfig.json                             # 2. type-check the page
npx vite build --config story/elnino-2026/vite.config.ts               # 3. the static page, story/elnino-2026/dist/
npx vite preview --config story/elnino-2026/vite.config.ts &           # 4. serve it on http://localhost:5181/
node story/elnino-2026/capture.mjs --url http://localhost:5181/ --out $JOB/work/frames/final \
  --mp4 $JOB/out/calcofi_elnino_2026_30s.mp4 --poster $JOB/out/calcofi_elnino_2026_poster.png
```

Look at single moments without rendering everything:

```sh
node story/elnino-2026/capture.mjs --url http://localhost:5181/ --out $JOB/work/shots --shots 0,10.6,23.5,26.2,29.9
```

Every string on screen, in order (run it after a change to the words, and check the list against the findings):

```sh
node story/elnino-2026/capture/strings.mjs http://localhost:5181/
```

It reads the DOM: the column, the pill, the legends, the strip, beat 7's callout, tag and record label. The labels drawn
inside the scene are not DOM text: the four place names, the isoline values (even isotherms as "16°", every degree of
difference as "+2"), the section's "+4" and "+8", and its depth marks "50 m", "100 m", "150 m".

Live, with hot reload: `npx vite --config story/elnino-2026/vite.config.ts`, then <http://localhost:5180/>. Space
pauses, ← → step a second, `?t=12.5` holds one moment.

The page fetches one thing from the network when it starts, and waits for it before the first frame: 24 terrain tiles
by range request from the GEBCO archive on `storage.googleapis.com/calcofi-db/bathymetry/`. Fonts, tokens and data are
in the bundle. After the page is ready a capture touches no network.
story/elnino-2026/render.sh (36 lines) 
#!/bin/zsh
# one command from the analysis database to the video:
#   story/elnino-2026/render.sh                      the deliverables: $JOB/out/calcofi_elnino_2026_30s.mp4, the poster
#                                                    (its last frame, lossless) and $JOB/out/frames/ (a frame per beat,
#                                                    pulled from the MP4, some also at phone width)
#   story/elnino-2026/render.sh <name> [capture.mjs args, e.g. --from 24 --to 30]
#                                                    a rough cut: $JOB/out/rough/<name>.mp4
# Rebuilds page/data/*.json, type-checks and builds the page, serves the build on its own port for the length of the
# capture (capture.mjs stops if the page's own check fails), encodes, probes.
set -euo pipefail
HERE=${0:A:h}; REPO=${HERE:h:h}
JOB=${JOB:-$HOME/_big/calcofi/story_elnino_2026-11}; PORT=${PORT:-5182}
cd $REPO
if (( $# )); then NAME=$1; shift; MP4=$JOB/out/rough/$NAME.mp4; EXTRA=("$@")
else NAME=final; MP4=$JOB/out/calcofi_elnino_2026_30s.mp4; EXTRA=(--poster $JOB/out/calcofi_elnino_2026_poster.png); fi

$HERE/build_data.sh $JOB > /dev/null
npx tsc -p story/elnino-2026/tsconfig.json
npx vite build --config story/elnino-2026/vite.config.ts | tail -1
npx vite preview --config story/elnino-2026/vite.config.ts --port $PORT --strictPort > $JOB/logs/preview_$NAME.log 2>&1 &
PREVIEW=$!; trap "kill $PREVIEW 2>/dev/null" EXIT
until curl -s -o /dev/null http://localhost:$PORT/; do sleep 0.3; done
rm -rf $JOB/work/frames/$NAME
node story/elnino-2026/capture.mjs --url http://localhost:$PORT/ --out $JOB/work/frames/$NAME --mp4 $MP4 "${EXTRA[@]}"
ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_name,profile,pix_fmt,width,height,r_frame_rate,nb_frames:format=duration,size -of default=nw=1 $MP4

if [[ $NAME == final ]]; then   # a frame per beat (two for beats 6 and 7), from the MP4 itself; four of them at phone width
  F=$JOB/out/frames; rm -rf $F; mkdir -p $F
  for spec in b1_cruises:0.5 b2_normal:7.9 b3_map:10.6 b4_next_year:14.7 b5_difference:16.6 b6a_2021:19.4 b6b_2026:23.5 b7a_tilt:26.2 b7b_section:29.9; do
    ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -ss ${spec##*:} -i $MP4 -frames:v 1 $F/${spec%%:*}_t${spec##*:}.png
  done
  for n in b1_cruises_t0.5 b3_map_t10.6 b5_difference_t16.6 b6b_2026_t23.5 b7b_section_t29.9; do
    ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i $F/$n.png -vf scale=390:-2 $F/phone390_$n.png
  done
  ls $F
fi
